articleTitle: Bees Swarm Optimization Based Prediction of Machined Fatigue Failure
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Artificial intelligence approach is now able to anticipate fatigue failure of machined components based on elementary key numbers without the need for professional knowledge of evaluation processes. In this paper, we develop a meta-heuristic approach for the prediction of defects using Bees Swarm Optimisation (BSO) in machined components. The study mainly predicts the fatigue failure by training the BSO experimentally with the training datasets. The three most essential input variables are the load stress, the hardness of the material, and the size of the fatal flaw (KD). In the context of fatigue testing, the only outcomes that may be determined are failure or non-failure. In this investigation, a single data set is generated for each specimen that is examined. When a full fracture has occurred at a given stress level, fracture surface analysis estimates the size of the deadly flaw that has formed. The architecture and hyperparameters of the neural network are cross-validated using a K-fold technique in order to get the highest possible prediction accuracy. After all is said and done, a cautious mean fatigue failure prediction accuracy of 92% is achieved.

articleTitle: Utilizing Recurrent Neural Networks for Sentiment Analysis of Financial News to Enhance Market Prediction and Investment Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In this study, an attempt was made to analyze the prospect of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) in carrying out sentiment analysis of financial news in order to improve market prediction and advancement in investment plans. Thus, employing developed NLP methods and neural networks, the study purpose is to develop an automatic solution for identifying the sentiment of financial news articles. The approach that is going to be used includes the data acquisition of great volume of financial news, the data preprocessing, the model training using BiLSTM with BERT embeddings for the sentiment analysis and the combination of the sentiment scores with the other standard financial figures in order to create the novel hybrid market predictor model. The comprehensive analysis shows a high increase in the accuracy of sentiment classification and market prediction and a higher efficiency of the hybrid model over traditional ones. Feedback from the financial analysts substantiates the applicability of the presented system describing it as convenient, precise, and compatible with other systems. In regards to the concerns of the study, hypotheses preoccupy the question of data quality as well as the interpretability of models, focusing on ethical concerns. Finally, the study proves that sentiment analysis based on RNN can give a significant contribution to the illumination of financial activities and help to enhance the effectiveness of the financial investment decision-making process.

articleTitle: A Scalable Privacy Preservation Block Chain-Based Method for Smart Healthcare System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In this study, we propose a scalable privacypreserving blockchain mechanism for smart healthcare systems. The rapid digitization of medical data has made security, scalability, and privacy vital. This approach minimizes risks associated with sensitive healthcare information by utilizing the decentralized architecture of blockchain to create a secure, transparent, and efficient healthcare information management platform. The system showed an increase in transaction throughput, a reduction of the latency, and an enhancement in energy efficiency compared with traditional approaches through simulations. Moreover, state-of-the-art cryptographic approaches provided strong privacy protection by reducing the risk of data leaks and malicious access. Smart contract implementation further optimized operations by facilitating secure and automated healthcare workflows. This method solves the growing issues in the area of managing healthcare data while delivering a much more scalable, secure, and patient-centric solution for contemporary healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in Agriculture: Cotton Leaf Disease Identification Using CNNs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This research proposes a new methodology for detecting cotton leaf diseases by Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The proposed system uses high-quality images of cotton leaves to identify diseases, including bacterial blight, curl virus, and fungal infection, with minimum human intervention. Thus, the study concerns dataset preparation, model architecture design, training, and evaluation. This CNN model was trained at an accuracy of 95.04% and validation accuracy of 84.38%, which suggests it can be used for disease detection. The test dataset evaluation's precision, recall, and F1 scores were reported as 80%, 79%, and 79%, respectively. Finally, these results demonstrate the potential of CNNs in process automation for diagnostic purposes and their contribution to precision agriculture. Future work could reduce model generalization, use regularization techniques, and increase the dataset's size.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-SVM Approach for Time-Series Activity Recognition Using Wearable Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Wearable electronics generate copious amounts of time-series data that are highly valuable in understanding user activity and physiological state. However, the use of this data for accurate activity classification poses a challenge thanks to issues of dimensionality, noise, and temporal correlation. This work proposes a combined pipeline for the FVC2006 databases using CNN for feature extraction and SVM for classification to overcome these challenges. Using the UCI Human Activity Recognition dataset of accelerometer and gyroscope data with six groups of activities we tested the proposed methodology. The CNN-SVM pipeline achieved a higher accuracy of 92.5 % in comparison to CNN (88.4 %) individually and SVM (79.2%). The classifications within all the activity classes were well-done with statistically similar scores of precision at 91.8%, recall at 92.0%, and F1-score at 91.9%. Misclassifications for comparable activities included “Upstairs” versus “Downstairs,” a misclassification rate of 4.5 percent, and “Standing” versus “Lying,” a misclassification rate of 3.8 percent. The resultant feature extraction was shown with the help of t-SNE map where inter class distance was found to be 88.5% and intra class distance was only 12.7%. From the earlier training and validation curves we see that both these curves gave us good indication of the model converging and validation accuracy of 92.3%. In fact, this paper presents the CNN-SVM as a highly efficient approach to dealing with certain related intricacies involved in time-series data for activity recognition in healthcare and fitness monitoring. Future prospects will focus on online implementation and learning technologies for different sorts of data.

articleTitle: Enabling Smart Manufacturing Through Big Data and IoT Integration: A Paradigm Shift in Industrial Processes
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Big Data and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies are being adopted in conventional manufacturing industries to shape processes into Smart Manufacturing Systems. Thus, this research investigates an integrated approach to deploying Big Data and IoT for improving process performance, product quality, and sustainability in industries. Two main techniques used in the methodology are as follows: It uses IoT sensors and devices to acquire data from the field in real-time, as well as huge volume storage systems like Hadoop to collect data from multiple sources and apply the data analytics process, which includes machine learning algorithms. Technologically driven solutions are connected for predictive maintenance and the corresponding change of process sequences and for flexible adjustment to changing circumstances. The success highlighted by this paper include a 66.7% reduction in production time loss, a 70% decrease in defects, and 30% decline in energy consumption per unit. Thus, a better inventory turnover along with a decrease in the order delivery cycle contributed to a more efficient supply chain and better protection of data guarded by efficiently developed cybersecurity. With issues like integration of old systems and data security, this framework presents the suite of how to modernize the process of manufacturing in a way that is both secure and efficient. The findings of this study emulate the opportunities of Big Data and IoT in creating a favourable environment for competitiveness, sustainability and customer orientation for the industrial domain thereby forming the premise for the evolution of smart manufacturing in the future.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Nipah Virus Infection Using Convolutional Neural Networks: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Nipah virus infection is a lightning-fast, high-lethality zoonotic disease that is significantly important from a public health perspective. Diagnosis of Nipah virus infection as early and precisely as possible is critical for effective intervention and prevention. This research presents the application of a deep learning technique, namely CNN, in detecting Nipah virus infection using medical imaging data. The proposed work introduces a state-of-the-art CNN architecture that leverages its efficient feature extraction and classification competencies to achieve dependable detection performance. All medical images used in this dataset were labeled and pre-processed for uniformity and quality, both for training and validation. Augmentation of data and tuning of hyperparameters optimized the training of the model. This yields an overall accuracy of classification of 87%. Though the overall loss can be relatively lower at about 11%, the model shows consistency in all its validation metrics, hence strong enough for infection pattern detection. These findings indicate that CNNs could be a diagnostic tool in detecting Nipah virus infections, thus enabling quicker and more efficient decision-making on the clinical front. Though the approach is scalable, it is widely adaptive for broader applications in infectious disease diagnostics. There are, however, acknowledged challenges with dataset limitations and generalization to real-world scenarios, pointing toward opportunities for further research to advance such accuracy and reliability. The study has concluded that deep learning-based models, such as CNN, hold tremendous potential to improve early detection of infection with the Nipah virus, eventually controlling the disease's spread and improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Towards Clinical Decision Support: CNN-SVM Models for Kidney Tumor Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Kidney cancer is listed among the leading causes of cancer deaths and that is why accurate staging of the disease and early diagnosis is so crucial. This research introduces a hybrid framework combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Support Vector Machines (SVM) for the classification of kidney tumors into four categories: Some of these are Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma (ccRCC), Papillary Renal Cell Carcinoma (pRCC), Chromophobe Renal Cell Carcinoma (chRCC), Benign Kidney Tumors. The CNN carried out feature extraction in an automatic manner, while the strength of the SVM was in classification using its impressive decision boundaries. Using the proposed model, the experiments were carried out on the 4000 labelled images of kidney tumor with the average accuracy of 93.75% which clearly outperforms standalone CNN with the accuracy of 91% as well as classic SVM with hand-crafted features equal to 85%. The proposed model provided precision equal to 94% in case of ccRCC, 91% for pRCC, 90% for chRCC, a well as 96% in case of Benign Tumor; while the recall of the model precisely unfolded as 92%, 89%, 88% and 94% respectively. The F1-scores ranged between 89 per cent and 95 per cent and suggested good consistency across all the parameters. Based on the confusion matrix results, there was little crossover between the two types of renal cancers, as well as between ccRCC and pRCC especially with 20 false positives and 18 false negatives. The ROC curve analysis also showed that the AUC for four classes being 0.94, 0.91, 0.90 and 0.96 respectively. The results further prove the performance of the CNN-SVM system of handling multi-Class imbalance and achieving high diagnostic performance. This paper demonstrates its applicability as a clinical decision support tool, aspiring to enhance the diagnostic results and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Wavelet & Transfer Learning Based Prosthetics Gestures Control
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The combination of Discrete Wavelet Transform denoising and transfer learning provides an effective approach for the categorization of electromyography data in prosthetic control. Electromyography data, frequently influenced by noise and complexity, are enhanced using discrete wavelet transform denoising, which separates essential characteristics while attenuating interference. The denoised signals are transformed into images via Continuous Wavelet Transform and subsequently input into a fine-tuned pre-trained AlexNet deep learning model for feature extraction. The characteristics are utilized to train a shallow classifier, forming a hybrid model that integrates the advantages of wavelet preprocessing with transfer learning. The model attains a test accuracy of 94.4% and a training accuracy of 100%, surpassing conventional approaches in both precision and efficiency. This scalable and adaptable system offers potential for real-time prosthetic control, improving the reliability and functionality of assistive devices.

articleTitle: Automated Skin Tone Classification Using InceptionV3: Enhancing Accuracy and Inclusivity in Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The study describes the skin tone classification into four categories, such as dark, light, mid-dark, and mid-light, using the machine learning of InceptionV3.The objective of this work was to improve the accuracy and fairness of automatic skin tone classification. The model has achieved 820 overall accuracy when trained and tested on the dataset containing 7,166 images. Performance metrics such as precision, recall, and fl-score were used to understand how this model performs across diverse skin tones. The results are that the best classes from the model are “dark” and “mid-dark”, with precisions, recalls, and fl-scores of 0.91, 0.92, and 0.92 and 0.92, 0.79 and 0.85, respectively. While for the class “light,” the performance was somewhat lower, with a precision of 0.79 and recall of 0.87, thus giving an fl-score of 0.83, the lowest metrics concerned the “mid-light” class, which had a precision of 0.63, recall of 0.66, and an fl-score of 0.64. Both the macro-averaged and weighted-average scores of the metrics were 0.81 and 0.82, respectively, which underlines the model's effectiveness balance across skin tones. In fact, the study emphasizes the promise of the InceptionV3in the classification of skin tones and points to some shortcomings, most especially the light skin tone. This work has to be improved in the future by enhancing model performance toward balanced skin tone classification, handling biases of the model, and expansion of the dataset for applicative usefulness in real world scenarios.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Malaria Diagnostics with CNNs: Automated Blood Smear Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Malaria remains one of the acute global health concerns; thus, its early and valid diagnosis plays a crucial role in effective treatment and control. Deep learning, of recent origin, especially Convolutional Neural Networks, provides exciting applications in automating and improving malaria detection. It proposes a CNN-based classification method, specifically designed for blood smear image classification capable of differentiating between malaria-infected and uninfected samples with remarkable correctness of 92.61% and reasonably low loss of 0.2025. In the proposed model, it availed the capability of CNN in gaining features to be able to capture the minute difference in cell morphology along with other minute features, which are very critical for malaria detection. The network has learned from a dataset with labeled data of blood smear images by training and evaluating. It reflects quite a lot of robustness and precision. The model herein is carefully crafted in architecture and optimization techniques with regard to challenges, such as variability in shape, size, and staining of cells common in microscopy-based approaches for malaria diagnosis. This approach massively cuts down on the level of manual intervention needed by trained professionals and also represents a scalable solution for deployment in low-resource settings where malaria prevalence is highest. Results indicate high accuracy and reliability of CNN-based detection of malaria; hence, it may be considered an important tool in global health initiatives looking for ways to cut mortality rates due to malaria. Therefore, further refinements and validations with larger and more varied datasets should be recommended to improve the adaptiveness of the model across different regions and imaging techniques.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fraud Detection Systems with Sequential Feature Analysis CNN and SVM Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Fraud detection in financial transactions has become one of the most challenging challenges because of the increased implementation of technological payment systems and the complexity of fraud schemes. The current work proposes a novel CNN-SVM model in handling the issues of identifying fraudulent activities in highly imbalanced datasets where the actual fraudulent transactions are as low as 0.3 % of the total. The hybrid method uses CNNs for capturing temporal and localized patterns from transaction sequences and the, patterns are accurately classified into fraudulent and non-fraudulent by using SVMs. The experimental evaluation has been conducted on a large transaction dataset with more than one million records. The hybrid model achieved 96.7%, outcompeting traditional models such as Logistic Regression (84.3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and Random Forest (88.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). It demonstrated higher recall rate (91.2%) and Fl-score (90.3%); it met the primary objective of lowering false negatives in fraud detection. The results further confirmed that the proposed hybrid model, CNNs improved the recall rate by 2.9 % and Fl-score by 2.6% in comparison to the individual CNNs, which indicates that the proposed model successfully the handle the unbalanced data. The hybrid model achieved computational efficiency suitable for practice since the time per inference was only 0.30 milliseconds. To this end, these investigation results demonstrate the utilization of the DL method in combination with the ML method, to address the limitations of each technique. By following the presented concept of utilizing a hybrid framework, today's financial systems can set a paradigm for scalable, precise, and efficient decision-making for fraud detection. Future expansions might examine how other non-supervised learning methods can also help decrease reliance on labeled images.

articleTitle: Optimizing Brain Tumor Diagnosis Through Hybrid Deep Learning and Multi-Modal Image Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The accurate detection of brain tumors is very important in order to make proper diagnosis and treatment planning. The combination of MRI with CT scans results in multi-modal medical imaging that is complementary and, therefore allows for further analysis. Unfortunately, in conventional fusion methods, information is often lost, and feature representation is suboptimal. In this paper, we introduce a novel hybrid deep learning framework consisting of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for spatial feature extraction and transformers for addressing long-term dependency. This work proposes a method of fusing multimodal imaging data to optimally improve tumor detection accuracy. The BraTS dataset MRI (T1, T2, FLAIR) and CT images were used for experimental evaluations. Our proposed model yielded the highest per-image accuracy of 93.6%, outperforming both the state-of-the-art U-Net model (85.2%) and PCA-based fusion techniques (78.5%). Moreover, the model was precise (92.4%), recall (91.8%), and f1-score (92.1%), and the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) was 90.7%. The robustness of the tumor versus non-tumor cases is confirmed using Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis, yielding an area under the curve of 0.96. Attention heatmap based qualitative analyses indicated the ability of the model to localize on a tumor region and found the fusion of the most important features from both modalities. The model converged stably within 30 epochs, as backed up by training and validation loss curves. The results of this study demonstrate the promise that hybrid deep learning frameworks hold for furthering multimodal medical imaging and establishing a new benchmark detection rate for brain tumors.

articleTitle: Analysis of Isotonic Calibration on Gaussian Naïve Bayes Performance for Guitar Chords Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Music recognition and recommendation is an area of machine learning which is gaining popularity by the day amongst interdisciplinary researchers. Guitar chord classification problem has been making rounds in machine learning enthusiasts for music recognition and recommendation models. Fundamentals of guitar playing and learning often includes the knowledge about guitar strings and chords etc. Going one step deeper, the domains like music recognition and music recommendation systems are evolving at a very fast pace. In this paper, we have worked on Guitar chord classification problem which has been explored and experimented in more than one dimension for music recognition and recommendation models. The preprocessing of guitar chords audio into numerical data is computationally extensive. During the preprocessing stage the harmonics are generated in large numbers and the effect of higher order harmonics is explored in some previous works. In this paper we have evaluated the Brier score losses of the Gaussian Naïve bayes algorithm for guitar chord classification problem for two sets of harmonics count. Further, the isotonic calibration is done on the classification problem and the experimental results are obtained and presented in the results and discussion section. Isotonic calibration of Gaussian Naïve bayes shows great promise in the performance where it gives improved values of Brier score for both harmonics inclusion cases. The results are improved by up 5% even when the harmonics are included upto 9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> position.

articleTitle: Prediction of Welding Distortion Using Autoencoders with Thermal and Stress Data in Deep Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Various welding defects remain crucial challenges in manufacturing; particularly welding distortion degrades the structurality of welded components.. Predicting welding distortion using thermal and stress data, this work propounds a deep learning system using SSAE. The study hinges on the GTAW tool and the mild steel workpieces were chosen because they are widely used in industries. The values for model training were gathered from finite element simulations and experimental tests for thermal and stress parameters when welding differently. SSAE model was completed with the help of TensorFlowadoop preprocessing and analysis was done using the numpy, pandas. Training and evaluation were also performed on NVIDIA CUDA-Enabled GPU for improved computation. Finally, the proposed model of the research is static, dynamic, and sound, with a prediction accuracy of 98.2%, mean absolute error of 0.016 mm and root mean squared of 0.019 mm. Comparison of the proposed SSAE model with ANNs and SVMs showed higher accuracy of the SSAE model with similar amounts of data and fewer computations. The performance of the model was further verified for various unseen circumstances of heat input and material properties where the overall predicted errors did not exceed 4%. Such results suggest that the developed framework is rather good at generalization to various welding regimes. With the help of deep learning approaches in combination with high-dimensional thermal and stress data, this study provides a sound approach for the predictive modeling of welding distortion with immediate application in the context of intelligent manufacturing systems.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Learning and Random Forest-Based EyeSmart Framework for Enhanced Retinal Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In this paper, a novel hybrid approach called the EyeSmart Framework that combines deep learning-based feature extraction with an optimized random forest classifier for the multi disease retinal analysis is presented. The framework uses pre trained convolution neural networks (CNNs), like ResNet50, to extract retinal images features at a high level, and classify them using an improved random forest model at an enhanced random forest model using hyperparameter. The approach being proposed here is to address the challenges of high accuracy, interpretability, and computational efficiency for diagnosis of retinal disease. Our framework was extensively experimented on publicly available retinal disease datasets, and performance was compared against traditional and supervised deep learning methods. We show that the EyeSmart Framework results in an accuracy of 92.1% which is a substantial improvement over a CNN only baseline model (85.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and a conventional random forest classifier (82.3%). Further, the framework reports a precision of 91.5%, recall of 90.8% and F 1 score of 91.2% for diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and age related macular degeneration thus making it robust to detect all three diseases. The AUC-ROC score of 0.94 is further validation of its capacity to differentiate between diseased and non diseased cases in comparison to CNN with score of 0.89 and random forest with 0.87. The impact of various CNN architectures and random forest hyperparameters on performance is ablated in the study. Through Grad-CAM visualizations, we show that the critical regions for classification are located on the retina, improving the interpretability of the model. Based on the results, the EyeSmart Framework serves as a viable and interpretable approach to automated retinal disease diagnosis and can be extended to real world clinical applications.

articleTitle: Study of Deep Fake in Images and Videos using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape, advancements in AI and machine learning (ML) are transforming various industries. One of the most notable solicitations of ML is deepfake technology, which relies on deep learning, specialized subset of Machine Learning. Deepfakes enable the manipulating videos and images by swapping one person's face with another's. While some alterations are easily detectable, others can be much more difficult to identify, depending on the precision of the algorithms used. With the rise of generative adversarial networks (GANs), it has become increasingly easy to create highly realistic fake images and videos, leading to an increase in deceptive media circulating online. These forged visuals serve a range of purposes, from entertainment and financial gain to spreading misinformation or advancing political agendas. Because of their lifelike quality, deepfakes can easily mislead viewers. Recent studies have highlighted the growing impact of deepfake media on society, organizations, and communities. This paper investigates methods for detecting fake videos and images using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), aiming to develop a model that can effectively distinguish between genuine and manipulated content by training on both real and fake datasets.

articleTitle: Computational Intelligence Based Plant Health Management System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The agricultural sector faces significant challenges in ensuring crop health and productivity. One critical aspect is the timely detection and management of plant diseases, as well as the judicious application of fertilizers to optimize growth. In conventional method, labor is the key role for identification of affected leafs and usage of fertilizer. But the conventional method is human centric and it takes more time and less accurate system. In order to overcome the limitations of conventional method and to enhance the soil productivity this paper contains a novel solution: a Plant Leaf Disease Detection and Fertilizer Suggestor system utilizing machine learning and deep learning techniques. On a comparing several algorithms such as CNN, SVM, KNN, etc., the proposed work contains most efficient algorithm Convolution Neural Network CNN. The system aims to automate the process of identifying plant diseases and recommending appropriate fertilizers, thereby enhancing efficiency and accuracy in agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Multimodal Lung Cancer Diagnosis: Combining CT Image Features with Metadata Using CNN and RF
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer deaths it is, therefore, important to have accurate and timely diagnosis tools. This paper gives a dual approach through which we shall employ CNNs for feature extraction on the CT images of patients while incorporating the secondary structured metadata on the patient such as age and smoking history through the application of RF. The findings also reveal that the proposed hybrid model offers a higher accuracy than individual CNN and RF models. When validating the analyzed output of a publicly available dataset, the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid model was observed to be 93.1% better than CNN (89.5%) and RF (85.3%). The performance measure of precision and recall was 0.910 and 0.924 respectively and thus the ability to minimize the false positive and false negative cases, which is more important in the context of early cancer diagnosis. The F1-score of 91.7%, shows that the model is equally good at both precision and recall, although that the AUC-ROC of 0.95 shows its discriminative capability is slightly better t CNN: 0.92 and RF: 0.88. For the malignant instances, the F1-scores calculated were 0.91, while for benign cases, the F1-scores obtained were 0.92 which supports the evidence of this model's robust state irrespective of the classifications. The feature importance analysis revealed that image features extracted by CNN accounted for about 70% of the total classification accuracy while 30% belonged to metadata with different modalities emphasizing the importance of the fusion of the multimodal data.. The studies thus establish the hybrid model for a dependable, interpretable, and scalable diagnostic tool for lung cancer diagnosis. The future studies might expand this approach to other disorders and evaluating the applicability of the method to real-world clinical settings.

articleTitle: Hybrid Ant-Bee Colony Algorithm for Signal Representation in Real-Time AI Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Several attempts have been made to develop appropriate signal representation in real-time AI applications using different hybrid algorithms, such as the Hybrid Ant-Bee Colony Algorithm. It combines ant colony optimization with bee colony optimization algorithms, which would be more capable of dealing with complex and dynamic signal data effectively. Specifically engineered for real-time AI in terms of signal representation accuracy, response speed, and flexibility, the HABC is well-matched to pattern recognition tasks such as data classification and signal demising. This algorithm uses a hybrid memory structure that consists of local and global memories to keep important signal information for retrieval. Local memory is responsible for learning and memorizing changes between signal time steps, while global learns a preserved version across the iterations. HABC adopts a parameter adjustment mechanism adaptable to the signal program of variant scenarios without frequent artificial intervention.

articleTitle: Smart Harvesting with AI: Analyzing Orange Ripeness Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Support Vector Machines
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Detection of orange ripeness is an important part of modern precision agriculture to achieve optimum harvesting, decreased postharvest losses and better orange quality. In this paper, based on the feature extraction ability of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and superior classification power of Support Vector Machines (SVMs), we present a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network - Support Vector Machine (CNN - SVM) framework for automated orange ripeness classification. The proposed model was trained and tested on a custom dataset of 5,000 labeled orange images, categorized into three ripeness stages: unripe, ripe, and overripe. Experimental results demonstrated that the CNN-SVM framework achieved an impressive classification accuracy of 97.5%, significantly outperforming standalone CNN (accuracy: 95. Our proposed approach achieved an accuracy of 85.6% and outperformed baseline eyewitness based models (accuracy: 76.2%), Support Vector Machine Convolutional Neural Networks (accuracy: 81.8%) and traditional SVM models (accuracy: 85.4%). The CNN-SVM model achieved precision and recall values of 96.7% and 97.3%, respectively, for distinguishing ripeness categories with minimum misclassifications, and comparison of the model with alternative methods like LSTM, Federated Learning CNN, CNN-RF and, RF validated its effectiveness in classifying ripeness categories. Our proposed approach also displayed a high area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.98, indicating potent discriminatory power. The analysis of confusion matrix shows very minimal misclassification and occurs between adjacent ripeness stages. Findings show the CNN-SVM framework represents an efficient, scalable, and accurate method for real time ripeness detection and actionable insights for the farmer to optimize harvesting decisions. As the future research, the model will be deployed to real world scenarios through IoT based systems in order to improve smart agricultural practices and increase productivity in citrus industry.

articleTitle: Utilizing Transforming Portfolio Management Through Automation Using Advanced Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for Optimized Investment Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This paper focuses on the future possibility of enhancing the applications of DRL in autonomously managing a portfolio for better investment plans. Having used past financial data and a highly developed case of DRL, the proposed system shows better performance compared to conventional investment strategies and indices. This process includes data gathering from the financial databases, the steps of preprocessing and feature extraction, and the use of the DQN structure. After that, the system's training and validation are done by a finite portion of real-world data and a large number of synthesized data to improve stability. The result shows that the new method achieves superior cumulative return, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, and annualized volatility; therefore, it suggests that the proposed system can flexibly predict the fluctuating stock market trends and make appropriate investment decisions. Thus, the present research adds importance to the use of DRL in improving return potential and risk management in portfolio management. Thus, this study adds to the existing literature and practice by allowing for the automation of the optimization and testing for investment solutions at a larger scale, while opening up opportunities for future developments in the application of financial technology and investment tools.

articleTitle: Data Mining Techniques for Predicting Energy Demand in Smart Grids: Optimizing Consumption and Production
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The growing complexity of renewable energy systems and the smarter grid has also made energy management a major issue. Precise forecasting of energy demand remains one of the most critical factors for effective energy utilization and generation, concern, dependability, and cost-efficiency. In this research, we present state-of-art data mining methods for predicting the energy demand in smart grids. In view of this, this study uses decision tree, support vector machines and neural network to establish models from historical energy consumption data as well as weather and user behavior patterns to predict the consumption accurately. The authors proposed architecture is meant to work with large streams of data in real-time to support dynamic control of energy loads and other demand response methodologies. Additionally, the research measures the effectiveness of feature reduction, dimension reduction, and clustering in enhancing the energy plans' predictive models. These methods do not only improve predictive capability but also help in designing energy distribution and storage systems. The results emphasize on the necessity of context-specific data mining solutions for digital smart grids, managing their specific problems. This study will be useful to energy suppliers and governments to build foundations for effective and practicable energy utilization in the smart grid environment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Employee Retention with AI: Predictive Analytics and Decision Support Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Maintaining a competitive advantage over their respective rivals depends on companies giving PADS (Predictive Analytics and Decision Support Systems) top priority. Conversely, experts in human resources often find it difficult to predict, from the current data, the expectations of employees. This work targets an original PADSS idea, Deep Decision Tree (DDT), with an aim of extracting already existing data. The authors of this work used the DDT method since it is efficient in handling big datasets. By means of an analysis of a range of data including publicly employed individuals, companies, and products that make use of technology, this paper aims to show how DDT could be able to better fulfill the employment requirements of the future. When compared to other approaches regarded to be quite conventional, the DDT method provides better accuracy and scalability. Professionals in the field of human resources can then use this data to make well-informed decisions about the configuration of digital workforce. This work significantly advances the field by laying a fresh basis for PADSS by means of advanced machine learning techniques.

Author Keywords: Predictive Analytics and Decision Support Systems

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Diabetic Foot Ulcer Detection with Hybrid CNN-SVM Models: An Accurate and Scalable Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: A major complication of diabetes, Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) are recognized by significant health outcomes when detected early. In this work, we propose the novel hybrid CNN-SVM model for accurate and scalable DFU detection that combines feature extraction strengths of deep learning and reliable classification power of machine learning. We evaluate the proposed model on the publicly available DFUC2021 dataset of 5000 annotated DFU images and that are split into 60%, 20% and 20% training, validation and testing set respectively. Or, this hybrid approach demonstrated a stunning accuracy of 94.5% which surpassed both the standalone CNN model with 91.2% specificity, and the traditional SVM classifier with handcrafted features at 82.5%. In addition, it exhibits higher precision (93.2%), recall (93.8%), F1 score (93.5%) and on an AUC - ROC of 0.98, attesting to its ability to discriminate between DFU and non - DFU cases better. To implemented the CNN component, based on the ResNet-50 architecture, for extracting deep hierarchical features and the SVM classifier with RBF kernel for generating robust decision boundaries thereby reducing over fitting and improving generalization. Experimental results, along with confusion matrix analysis and ROC curve evaluation, show that the model has potential to be applied in clinic, achieving significant reduction of false positives and false negatives. Proposed hybrid approach to detect DFU proposes a scalable and efficient solution for DFU detection that can be deployed for real world healthcare and telemedicine applications. Further work will investigate merging explainable Al techniques to add interpretability to the model and extending the model for multi class DFU classification.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Machine Learning Fusion for Sleep Apnea Diagnosis and Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Sleep apnea is a widespread sleep disorder with life threatening conditions like cardiovascular diseases as well as cognitive impairments. Given that accurate classification of its types (obstructive, central, and mixed) is essential to treatment, a thorough physical examination is highly essential during the initial visit. In this study, we propose to design a hybrid model consisting of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and Support Vector Machines (SVMs) for classification using physiological data like Electrocardiograms (ECG), pulse oximetry (SpO2), etc. The overall accuracy of the model is 93.0% and precision, recall, and F1-score were 92.4%, 93.0%, and 92.7%, respectively. Its strong discriminatory ability is also validated by the ROC-AUC score of 0.960. Obstructive apnea (95.3%) has the highest accuracy, central apnea (92.8%) has the second highest and mixed apnea (90.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) has the third highest accuracy. A comparative analysis demonstrates that the hybrid approach further decreases misclassification rates and improves generalization to apnea types compared to standalone classifiers. We perform feature importance analysis which reveals SpO2 variations and heart rate variability (HRV) as the two most important predictors that characterize desaturations and cardiovascular patterns indicative of apnea events. The model shows strong performance, but is limited in generalizability to unseen populations and involves a computational overhead. We propose a CNN-SVM hybrid model which we find to be reliable and cost effective to perform automated sleep apnea classification. This suggests that by utilizing physiological data, this approach can aid in the development of real time diagnostic tools, lower the dependence on polysomnography that is both time and resource intensive, and enhance personalized treatment strategies.

articleTitle: Fintech Innovation Through Incubators: Exploring the Impact of Technology Business Incubators on Financial Technology Ventures
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: As the FinTech sector is changing rapidly, startups face particular difficult like regulatory hurdles, technological complexities and market entry barrier. This paper discovers a vital role of Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) in promoting creativity within the Financial Technology (FinTech) sector. Technology Business Incubator is a crucial platform for supporting these startups by providing them with mentorship, critical resources, networking and funding opportunities. Incubators can facilitate the expansion and scaling of FinTech ventures with the combination of various services like business development, administrative and technical which will help them transform creative ideas into viable financial solutions. This paper also discusses the dimensions of incubator support, the ecosystem of collaborative innovation that incubators cultivate and the role of incubators in FinTech startup development that have arisen from these kinds of settings. Additionally, this paper also highlights the future possibilities of incubators within the FinTech industry, evolving services, focusing on emerging trends and the overall effect of incubator involvement on sustained prosperity in the financial technology industry. So, this work explains how incubators helps in contributing to the growth of FinTech innovation and influence the financial services industry's future.

articleTitle: Enhanced ECG Signal Analysis Using Hybrid CNN-LSTM and Augmentation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The nature and timely nature of the detection of the arrhythmias are critical in preventing severe cardiac repercussions like stroke or sudden cardiac death. First, this research proposes a deep learning model that integrates convolutional neural network (CNN) as well as recurrent neural network with long short-term memory (LSTM) for the classification of arrhythmias from ECG data. CNN component is responsible for extracting geographical features whereas LSTM identifies temporal dependency, creating a good base for understanding consecutive ECG signals. MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database was used for training and validation, showing near perfect performance of the model with an accuracy of 98.2%, precision of 97.8%, recall of 98.5%, and F1-score of 98.1%. Preprocessing measures such as normalization, R-peak detection for signal segmentation and augmentation ensured data accuracy and generality. The comparative study with standalone models revealed that the proposed hybrid architecture outperformed CNN (accuracy: 92. Traditional classifiers, like SVM, SVR, attained 85.3% accuracy, while the universal LSTM model achieved an impressive 94.2%, RNN 80.5% and GRU 7%. This was further supported by ROC curves where AUC of the model was high on five different classes of arrhythmia. For extensibility and compliance with clinical decision-making processes, forecaster was incorporated into the framework with SHAP which ensure that forecasts are explicable and believable to many health care professionals.

articleTitle: Advancing Agricultural Sustainability: Machine Learning-Driven Insights for Optimized Crop Yield Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Sustainable agriculture is crucial for addressing global challenges related to food security, resource efficiency, and environmental preservation. This study examines the potential of machine learning (ML) in forecasting crop production to enhance decision-making and promote sustainable agricultural practices. The research investigates advanced machine learning techniques, including Multilayer Perceptron Artificial Neural Networks (MLP ANN), Decision Trees, Voting Classifiers, and YOLO models, for accurate agricultural yield prediction. These models employ several data sources, encompassing climatic conditions, soil properties, and agricultural practices. Among the assessed models, the MLP ANN achieved a notable accuracy of 91%, illustrating its efficacy in predicting agricultural production. The results demonstrate how these predictive models aid farmers and policymakers in optimizing resource allocation, reducing waste, and aligning agricultural inputs with expected outputs, thereby decreasing environmental impact and improving economic outcomes. Essential insights highlight the effectiveness of data-driven methods in reducing uncertainty and enhancing agricultural productivity. The paper finishes by identifying barriers to the widespread adoption of ML-based solutions and outlining opportunities for integrating these technologies into sustainable agricultural systems, so offering a framework for future implementation.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Diagnosis: A CNN-SVM Framework for Identifying COVID-19 in Chest Radiographs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The current COVID-19 outbreak has clearly shown that accurate, rapid and sensitive diagnostic tools are need of the hour. Despite the fact that RT-PCR assays remain an acknowledged standard, the observed limitations of these methods make further diagnostic tests desirable. This research proposes a CNN-SVM model for the CXRs classification as COVID-19 positive or negative combining the CNN feature extraction and the exhaustive classification performance of SVMS. The efficiency of the proposed framework has been evaluated using the public available CXR dataset, which was made augmented to address class imbalance issue. The cumulative model CNN-SVM achieved the best performance of 93.2% which is much higher than that of the separate CNN and SVM having achieved 89.5% and 85.2% accuracies respectively. The hybrid model exhibited enhanced precision (92.5%), recall (93.8%), and F1-score (93.1%) relative to the CNN-only model (precision: 88. Precision: 7%, recall: 90.2 %; F1 score: 89.4%. The AUC-ROC value for the proposed framework was 0.96, which illustrated that the COVID-19 positive and negative cases can be differentiated more accurately using the proposed framework than using only the CNN or SVM techniques, with an AUC-ROC of 0.92 for CNN and 0.88 for SVM. The training and validation curves of the losses gave a clear conviction of efficient learning with less overfitting, while the confusion matrix yielded 85% accuracy in COVID-positive cases and less misclassification. These results support the reliability and validity of the hybrid model when used in clinical contexts. Future work will focus on increasing the variety of datasets and finding ways to enhance pre-training approaches. The study leads to understanding CNN-SVM as efficient tool to apply artificial intelligence in COVID-19 diagnosis.

articleTitle: Enhancing Precision Agriculture with a CNN-RF Hybrid Model: A Case Study on Sunflower Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Disease classification in sunflower crops is an important step in mitigating the yield losses incurred because of high disease spread and improving agricultural productivity. In this paper we present a novel hybrid model that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and Random Forest (RF) for classification so as to leverage the complementary strengths of these techniques. The model was evaluated on a sunflower disease dataset containing 10,000 images across five classes: Downy Mildew, Rust, Leaf Blight, and Alternaria Leaf Spot are healthy. The hybrid CNN-RF model yielded an accuracy of 96.2 %, beating standalone CNN (93.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and RF (85.1%). Robustness and a tradeoff between false positives and false negatives are also demonstrated by the model, evidenced by the precision., recall, and F1 scores of 96.5%., 96.0%, and 96.2%, respectively. The performance in discriminative capability was excellent, with an AUC of 0.95 yielded from the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. A confusion matrix analysis showed that over 95% of cases were accurately classified, while the highest misclassification rate of only 3% was observed between Rust and Alternaria Leaf Spot. The hybrid model was thoroughly trained with minimal overfitting, as shown by the losses of 0.12 and 0.18., and ended with 98.2% and 96.2% final training and validation accuracies. Although with an inference time of 25ms per image, it would also be suitable for real-time agricultural uses. The results show that the CNN-RF hybrid model is a suitable, scalable., and efficient solution for automated sunflower disease detection with the potential to revolutionize precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Optimized Detection of Tomato Leaf Diseases via VGG16 Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The implementation of such a deep learning-based method in tomato leaf disease identification is presented in this research using the VGG16 neural network. The model was adapted to classify healthy and diseased tomato leaves into seven categories such as bacterial spot, early blight, and late blight, using transfer learning and fine-tuning techniques. Training, validation and testing on a comprehensive dataset, preprocessed to standard dimensions and augmented for robustness, was used. And though the VGG 16 based model was quite good, with training accuracy of 90.25% and validation accuracy of 88.86%. Precision, recall and F1 scores were 85.93%, 84.43% and 84.82%, respectively, were the key metrics. The results suggest strong generalization capability, little overfitting. Furthermore, the model was proven to have high accuracy at differentiating between different disease types, as further validated by the confusion matrix. The contributions in this study are to the field of precision agriculture with an automated, scalable solution for the early detection of tomato leaf diseases. These advancements could eliminate crop losses and increase productivity, which is again sustainable farming practice. The methodology proposed enables AI powered solution to be integrated within the agricultural process as a reliable tool for disease monitoring and control.

articleTitle: Leveraging Quantum Computing for Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis in Strategic Business Planning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This study examines the feasibility of quantum computing as a new approach to multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) in strategic business planning. Quantum algorithms can provide advantages over classical methods in solving complex decision-making tasks by leveraging unique quantum properties that include superposition, entanglement, and parallelism. These include drastically shortening computation times, increasing accuracy, and successfully solving large, interconnected decision spaces. Visual simulations and comparative analysis are carried out to show the advantages of quantum algorithms in the ability to solve multi-criteria problems. The outcomes show that the QDPA converges at a more rapid pace, with a smaller error margin, demonstrating the applicability and viability of quantum methods in intricate decision-making environments. This effort is vital as it leverages quantum computing as a compelling strategic business enabling technology by facilitating better analysis of costly complex decisions.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enhanced Wireless Communication Protocols for Ultra-Reliable and Low-Latency Applications in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In this study, we develop and evaluate machine learning enhanced wireless communication protocols to satisfy the ultra reliable and low latency requirements in smart city applications. In today's urban areas where smart technologies are increasingly incorporated, traditional wireless protocol limitations are obvious, especially related to its incapability to handle fluctuating traffic situations. The proposed methodology consists of a whole process that encompasses data collection, feature engineering, machine learning model development, protocol enhancement, and performance evaluation. We train multiple machine learning models using the key datasets including network traffic patterns and measurements of latency, and integrate them into the existing communication protocols. In particular, the results show a spectacular performance, achieving a latency of five milliseconds on average and a packet delivery ratio of 98%, which is far beyond the performance achieved by traditional protocols. Of special interest in this research is its contribution toward the design of adaptive communication systems that can support the burgeoning needs of smart urban environments, thus spurring new developments in the field of wireless communication technology.

articleTitle: AI-Driven MBA Programs for Personalized Learning and Skill Development for Future Business Leaders
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The possibility of including federal education (FL) into the master's degree in business administration programs is investigated in this paper in order to improve the personal learning and skills of forthcoming business leaders. The current educational system finds it difficult to adapt the traditional Master of Business Administration program to fit the demands of the corporate environment. Federated learning is based on the theory that one could distribute training models without a central database. One can provide this capacity using a technique of machine learning. This study intends to close a gap in the present Master of Business Administration curriculum by means of a fresh approach leveraging public education. This study seeks to identify how this method might be used to customise learning resources so that they satisfy the specific needs of every student while maintaining anonymity and security. This paper intends to understand the effects of FL-oriented self-learning on cognition and well-being by means of a mixed-method research comprising qualitative and quantitative data respectively. The results of the experiment will provide interesting information on the practicability and benefits of using state education under the Master of Business Administration degree. This study is supposed to be the foundation for significant changes in business education, hence ensuring that future business leaders have the tools needed to succeed in a professional transition.

articleTitle: Sensor Networks for Real-Time Air Quality Monitoring in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This requires ubiquitous sensor networks to monitor and instantaneously predict dangerous gas concentrations at ground level deployed within smart city environments. A sensor network is a collection of many distributed sensors that can be used together to gather data in real-time and from standard logs across an environment, generally allowing users to see, hear, or feel whether emissions are entering their air as they happen. Cities attaching these sensor networks can provide real-time air quality data for municipalities and citizens taking control of our health. It can analyze pollution hotspots, detect trends and patterns over time, and act as an early warning system for dangers. Such work creates a framework for interventions to be undertaken quickly and efficiently to reduce air pollution as soon as possible and work towards protecting residents' public health. Sensor networks can also provide historical data, which is necessary for tracking long-term trends and assessing how effective pollution control measures have been. Furthermore, this information can validate city-specific policies and exercise recommendations for reducing air pollution in smart cities. It will give decision-makers and citizens the data they must act on while making well-informed decisions for cleaner air in their cities.

articleTitle: Spatial-Sequential Analysis for Breast Cancer Diagnosis: Integrating CNN and LSTM Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Diagnosis of breast cancer is a extremely critical task in medical imaging, for which accurate and efficient computational methods are required. In this thesis, a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract spatial features and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to recognize sequential patterns improves breast cancer classification. Evaluation of the proposed model on benchmark mammography datasets shows that the model achieves an accuracy of 92.8 %, compared to standalone CNN (89.3 % and LSTM (85.2)). Precision wise, the hybrid approach received 92.3 to 88.7 and 84.9 for CNN and LSTM, respectively, and recall at 92.7, 89.1, and 85.5. Finally, the proposed hybrid model achieved an F1score of 92.5% that is the balanced tradeoff between precision and recall. In addition, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to validate the effectiveness of the model, which showed a high value of 0.96 for the AUC score for hybrid model compared with CNN (AUC 0.91) and LSTM (AUC 0.88) score that prove its ability to separate malignant and benign cases better than other models. The training and validation accuracy curves were plotted and we observed a steady improvement in both of them and training loss reduced from 0.60 to 0.10 and validation loss reduced from 0.65 to 0.15 showing that it is good at learning and generalization. Furthermore, these results prove that the CNN-LSTM hybrid model is a promising solution for automated breast cancer diagnosis through the ability to learn spatial and sequential features to help diagnose more accurately and robust manner. Future work involves improving interpretability through use of explainable AI techniques, as well as evaluation across larger datasets.

articleTitle: A Robust CNN-LSTM Framework for Sensitive and Specific Brain Tumor Classifications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Diagnosing brain tumor is a key medical challenge where identification of the tumor is crucial to determine an appropriate treatment methodology. In this paper, we present a new hybrid deep learning model that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to take advantage of spatial and temporal features on multimodal MRI scans to better diagnose classifying diseases. It combines a CNN component to extract high level spatial features and an LSTM component to encode temporal dependencies between MRI slice features, thereby making a robust diagnostic system. The model was trained and validated using the publicly available BraTS dataset, achieving an accuracy of 97.8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, sensitivity of 98.5%, and specificity of 97.3%, outperforming state-of-the-art models such as ResNet50 (accuracy: 95. It was compared to a NeXt 3D (accuracy: 96.5%, 91.3% sensitivity, 99.8% specificity) and VGG16 (accuracy: 94.7%, 94.9% sensitivity, 94.3% specificity). An ablation study revealed a contribution of each module: the accuracy of the standalone CNN module is 92.4%, the standalone LSTM module is 90.1%, and the accuracy of the proposed hybrid model is 94.0%. The model's focus on tumor regions was validated by Grad-CAM visualizations that improved its interpretability for clinical applications. Both why and how it performed were proven through statistical analysis including confidence intervals and paired t-tests of p < 0.01. Our resulting CNN-LSTM hybrid model is proven by data as a reliable and interpretable means of brain tumor diagnosis that provides high diagnostic accuracy while being clinically interpretable. The future work is to experiment with integrating attentions and larger data sets to improve performance and scalability.

articleTitle: Parallel Selective Meta-Heuristic Algorithms for Real-Time Non-Convex Optimization in Big Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: With big data in modern analytics becoming more common, a lot of it is real-time optimization, which is an essential problem. This is because big data requires efficient and accurate optimization methods, leading to developing parallel selective viable meta-heuristic algorithms for nonconvex optimization in large analytics. They can be used to find optimal solutions rapidly by merging the complementary advantages of meta-heuristics and parallel computing. Algorithms do this using an optimization process, but not always for the whole data set used, saving computational performance. As information is updated in real-time, its approach will constantly be improved, resulting in a better and more accurate solution. A parallel implementation of these algorithms makes them effective for real-time optimization using large datasets. However, the performance of big data analytics may be significantly improved by implementing these algorithms because they have achieved satisfactory results in a number of applications, including machine learning, data mining, and pattern recognition.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Meets Traditional AI: A Hybrid CNN-RF Model for Accurate and Explainable Skin Lesion Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In dermatology, the task of skin lesion classification is a very important one, for early detection and treatment of skin cancer. In this work, we propose a hybrid AI model where Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used for feature extraction and a Random Forest (RF) classifier for final decision making. We evaluate the proposed model on the ISIC dataset: images of multiple types of skin lesion (melanoma, benign nevi, seborrheic keratosis). Experimental results show that the hybrid CNN_RF model surpasses stand alone models in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, yielding an accuracy of 89.5%, precision of 88.9%, recall of 89.2% and F1 score of 89.0%; the standalone CNN and RF models resulted in accuracies of 85.3%, 78.6% respectively. The method proposed successfully strikes a good balance between feature learning and classification robustness, using the resultant model to provide better generalization. Finally, we perform qualitative analysis using Grad-CAM visualizations to motivate the model towards focusing on relevant lesion regions which improves interpretability. Moreover, the RF classifier also provides the feature importance insight to support clinical decision making. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, confirms that the model has a strong discriminative power with an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.92. The hybrid model shows stable learning without sharply decreasing the training set error; in other words, there is no strong overfitting of training data. The learning process also demonstrates stable training and validation accuracy curves and can be used in real applications. The results show that the CNN RF hybrid model is a promising solution for automated skin lesion classification which provides higher accuracy, interpretability and robustness.

articleTitle: Cataract Detection Using Transfer Learning on Fundus Images: A Deep Learning Approach for Automated Ophthalmic Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Early detection of cataracts is critical, since they are a leading cause of visual impairment worldwide and can be appropriately treated. A deep learning-based approach to cataract detection is presented using transfer learning with the ResNet-50 architecture in this study. Bulk preprocessing involving resizing, normalization, and data augmentation was performed on the Ocular Disease Recognition dataset comprised of 2, 290 labeled fundus images to ensure that robust training is possible. To perform evaluation of model performance, the dataset was split into training, validation and test sets. Fine tuning ResNet 50 for binary classification gave us an impressive accuracy of 90% with precision, recall and f1 scores of 0.89 each for both Cataract and Normal class respectively. Training, validation loss and accuracy curves analysis, confusion matrix and classification report analysis proved that the model offered great generalization and very low overfitting. Transfer learning could be a promising approach to empowe reliable, automated cataract diagnosis at scale and in a way that is accessible to primary care providers and patients.

articleTitle: Epileptic Seizure Prediction: A Comparative Analysis of LSTM and ANN Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Epileptic seizures, characterized by abnormal electrical discharges in the brain, pose significant challenges to individuals' health and quality of life. The accurate and timely detection of seizures is critical for effective treatment and prevention of severe consequences. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals, widely used for seizure monitoring, offer valuable insights into neural activity but require robust analysis techniques to identify seizures accurately. Leveraging advancements in machine learning and deep learning, this study investigates the performance of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks in classifying seizure and non-seizure activity using the UCI Epileptic Seizure Recognition dataset. The dataset was preprocessed through normalization, outlier handling, and feature scaling, ensuring data quality for effective model training and evaluation. Key metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and ROC-AUC scores, were employed to assess the models' performance comprehensively. The findings highlight that the ANN model outperforms the LSTM in terms of classification accuracy and computational efficiency, achieving an impressive ROC-AUC of 0.987. Its simpler architecture effectively captured the dataset's numerical features, leading to fewer misclassifications. In contrast, the LSTM model, with an AUC of 0.900, demonstrated limitations in handling the segmented EEG data, resulting in higher misclassification rates, particularly for seizure instances. However, its ability to model temporal dependencies makes it a promising approach for continuous EEG data analysis. This study underscores the importance of aligning model selection with dataset characteristics, emphasizing that while ANN offers robust performance for segmented EEG data, LSTM holds potential for tasks requiring sequential pattern recognition. The results contribute to advancing machine learning applications in epilepsy diagnosis and treatment.

articleTitle: Enhancing Academic Excellence Using a Data-Driven Approach for NIRF Ranking Improvement of Newly Established IITs
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the urgent need for better evaluation techniques in educational institutions, concentrating about 10 recently founded Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs). We point out that conventional bibliometric measures fall short of adequately expressing the research influence and capacities of these universities. In order to improve the rankings of these IITs in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF), we suggest a novel method to evaluate their academic output and impact using data analytics and altmetrics. Here we compare Scopus publishing figures against NIRF rankings over many years. Furthermore, we advocate a thorough evaluation strategy including social media metrics and other kinds of scholarly influence outside conventional references. Here we introduce ResNet-PSO, a deep learning technique whereby Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) is coupled with Residual Neural Networks (ResNet) to improve the accuracy and efficiency of our research. By means of ResNet-PSO for data analytics, we can obtain significant insights from extensive academic datasets, so augmenting a more complete knowledge of research trends and impact variables. Our work intends to provide academic institutions and legislators important insights to promote research quality and competitiveness by bridging the gap between current metrics and developing altmetrics.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Cardiovascular Diagnostics: Arrhythmia Detection with CNN and SVM
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Arrhythmia is characterized by abnormally beating heart a serious condition that the requires timely and accurate identification. In this study, a novel architecture consisting of both CNN and SVM has been designed and implemented for the classifier, for the diagnosis of arrhythmias based on the ECG inputs. The hybrid model combines applying CNN for feature extraction and employing SVM for classification to address subtle feature problems and class imbalance. The performance of the model was tested with the help of benchmark database called MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. The results of the experiments showed that the efficiency of the proposed hybrid CNN-SVM model was 94.7% more than the pure CNN (92.4%) and SVM (87.6%) models. The proposed hybrid model achieved high classification accuracy at 93.9%, recall of 92.8%, F1 measure of 93.3%, as well as an AUC-ROC of 0.96. Using the hybrid model, the underrepresented classes namely Bradycardia and Tachycardia have been successfully identified with recall scores of 91.2% and 89.8% respectively as against 85.4%, and 87.6% corresponding to the solo CNN. We found that the hybrid model shows much faster convergence in the training stage than the solo model; after 15 iterations, the hybrid model stability of the validation accuracy is achieved that takes 20 iterations for the solo CNN model. As the results estimated, the effectiveness of the proposed method is sufficiently high and proves its applicability for clinical practice, as well as their stability for the further usage. Future work will focus on further refining the model, testing it with more extensive data collections, and applying the techniques of explainable AI to enhance the paper's clinical applicability.

articleTitle: Unlocking Scholarly Insights Using Deep Learning-Based Evaluation Method for Research Impact Assessment in Academic Institutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: This paper addresses the academic institutions, especially the recently founded Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), who struggle to appropriately evaluate and communicate their research potential. We call attention to the shortcomings in the present evaluation techniques, especially the dependence on bibliometric data, which would not fairly represent the spectrum of scholarly contributions. Objectives: Using data analytics and altmetrics, our study suggests a complete strategy to assess the research impact and exposure of these institutions with an eventual aim of raising their positions in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF). We demonstrate how Scopus publishing data analysis and comparison with NIRF rankings can provide real-time insights into academic influence, hence augmenting conventional metrics. Methodology and Findings: Together with Firefly optimization, we also offer a new deep learning technique called Deep Belief Networks (DBN), which improves the precision of data analytics process. By use of DBN-Firefly optimization, we hope to find links and patterns in academic data thereby enabling academic institutions and legislators to make better decisions.

articleTitle: Exploring the Transition from 5G to 6G: Advancements in Ultra-Low Latency, High-Speed Connectivity, and AI-Driven Network Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This paper focuses on the evolution from 5G to 6G regarding progress in ultra-low latency, highly accessible networks., and AI-assisted adaptive networking. The paper also explains how 6G will transform wireless communication by reducing latency to near zero while attaining terabit per second data transfer rates. AI will enhance its effectiveness in network management by improving a self-organizing and adaptive system that will transform the efficiency and reliability of the networks. The argumentation of the research also touches upon such specific themes as spectrum management and usage of the terahertz band, possible issues include signal attenuation. The second area is energy efficiency enhancements, which should be primarily oriented toward sustainability, to support 6G innovation. The presented approach adopts AI models for the enhancement of network design and conducts simulations for performance comparison between 6G and 5G. The achieved outcomes show significant increases in latency, throughput, and energy efficiency which indicates 6G as a breakthrough solution for businesses that rely on real-time high-speed data services. Based on this knowledge, the study determines that 6G will be an instrumental in the future digital environment as it will unlock the potential of new innovative technologies like automotive systems, IoT, VR, and AR.

articleTitle: Efficient Colon Cancer Detection Using Transfer Learning with EfficientNet: A Deep Learning Approach for Enhanced Diagnostic Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Early detection is critical because colon cancer is a leading cause of cancer deaths worldwide. Traditional diagnostic techniques are invasive, expensive, and often inaccessible.
