They can detect and acquire physiological information, including heart rate, blood pressure, and oxygen levels, in a non-invasive and very timely manner. They can then transfer this information over to a secured database, where further analysis can be carried out and the data integrated into healthcare applications. The provision of objective and accurate data is one of the main properties of biometric sensors, as human errors and biases involved in self-reports by patients can be avoided. It allows health authorities to have more data available when making true and immediate decisions about how to proceed in terms of taking care of patients. Biometric sensors also provide additional security features, ensuring that only authenticated individuals have access to sensitive health data. This problem is even worse within the healthcare industry, as data privacy and security should be of utmost concentration. This means biometric sensors are continuously monitored over time, so in the case of an issue, it can be detected early and tracked sequentially through treatment plans. It is particularly advantageous for patients with chronic diseases or individuals in rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Study on Optimized Hardware Design for High Speed and Noise Resilient Bio Signal Transmission Using Chaotic Memristor-Capacitor Integrated Cryptosystem with RealTime Alarm System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Recent advancements in bio-signal transmission focus primarily on enhancing security. Memristor-based cryptosystems have gained attention due to the ability to introduce complex chaotic behaviors, which improve the encryption of bio-signals such as ECGs, making the transmission more secure. The Logistic-coupled Memristor (LCM) map, which combines discrete memristors with a one-dimensional (1D) chaotic logistic map which is used to increase the unpredictability and encryption strength of signals. The novelty of this paper is bio-signal communication through speed and intelligent noise cancellation. This article presents a study of hardware-based cryptosystem using Raspberry Pi 4 Model B as the main single-board computer with an integrated Logistics-coupled memristor coupled to a capacitor to reduce noise further. The system also takes advantage of this generation of Raspberry Pi because it has very high processing power and memory, making it suitable for exceptionally complex tasks of encryption and advanced noise filtering. The proposed review was furtherly improved with the use of LPF and HPF and signal transformation. The system has a real time alarm system that notifies medical personnel in case of any emergencies such as heart attacks. Previous realization has used ATmega328P microcontroller, which is used in Arduino Uno and Nano, allowing chaos encryption but with a limited range, slow processing, poor filtering of noise, and quite limited memory. This particular study just concerned optimizing transmission speed and noise filtering efficiency by having a capacitor in parallel with the Logistic Coupled Memristor (LCM) map to ensure the best solution for real-time bio-signal communication and alerting.

articleTitle: Predicting Solar Power Based on Machine Learning Approaches and Their Efficacy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The planning, administration, and operation of power systems depend on enhancing the forecasting accuracy of solar energy as it grows in popularity within the worldwide electric grid. However, the erratic and disorganised nature of solar energy data makes this a difficult process. To increase a forecasting accuracy of renewable energy, a number of approaches have been developed to date, including statistical methodologies, physical models, and AI techniques. Using weather data collected in Errachidia, Morocco, this research explores the use of several ML techniques for predicting solar power production. Different models, namely ANN, Ridge Regression, SVM, and KNN were employed to forecast solar energy output. Performance evaluation index; therefore, the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>_ score and the root mean standard error were used to assess the prowess of the different models. The findings showed that when it came to solar energy predictions, the ANN model was the most accurate, with a R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 99.93 and an RMSE of 0.08. In order to enhance energy management tactics, the results show that ML methods, especially ANN, may increase an accuracy of solar power projections.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Recognition in Real-Time Surveillance Using CNN and Transfer Learning with ResNet-50
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of real-time FER system implemented using CNN with transfer learning from ResNet-50 for surveillance video analysis. The system is designed to efficiently identify seven basic facial expressions: segment by real-time video frames in the form of Happy, Sad, Angry, Surprised, Disgusted, Fearful and Neutral. Since there are lighting changes, occlusion and diverse orientations of the face in surveillance environment, the utilization of pretrained ResNet-50 allows the system to perform well and properly distinguish facial expressions. The proposed method uses the transfer learning to fine tune the ResNet-50 on a large FER dataset and obtain good classification accuracy, precision, recall, F1-Score as well. Evaluation data prove that the suggested model yields a 96.2% recognition rate as well as high precision (97.9%) and recall (96.9) ratios. In addition, inference time works as low as at 35 ms per frame to achieve 28.5 FPS for real-time application. Further, the proposed model provides better accuracy as compared to the regular models like the VGGNet and InceptionNet, along with less computation time. This work gives a strong real-time technique to recognize the facial expression which is prepared for use in security and surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Harnessing EfficientNetB5 for Accurate Skin Disease Classification: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Skin diseases are best treated when detected at a very early stage and deep learning can be used to help in this identification process. In this work, an EfficientNet deep learning model is introduced to classify 10 types of skin diseases, such as Melanoma, Basal Cell Carcinoma, and Psoriasis. The proposed model has an overall accuracy of 87%, which shows high precision and recall for conditions such as Melanoma and Melanocytic Nevi (NV). Analysis of performance through a classification report and confusion matrix shows that although the model is accurate, there is still a problem in differentiating between Psoriasis & Lichen Planus and Seborrheic Keratoses. The results show that EfficientNet can be effectively applied for dermatological purposes and provide an effective approach to automated skin disease diagnosis. Some potential future work could enhance the model's capacity to distinguish between visually similar diseases and its applicability in clinical practice.

articleTitle: Mining Consumer Behavior Patterns in E-Commerce Using Apriori Algorithm and Sequential Pattern Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The consumer behaviour in e-commerce is the main focus of this research and data has been collected using Apriori Algorithm association rule mining method followed by the use of sequence analysis. The work applies real large transactional databases to generate the frequent items and the next sequences of the consumers’ buying habits. Looking at association and sequence mining in Python using MLxtend and Seq2Pat libraries named those consumer patterns that are relevant, for instance, smartphones often go hand in hand with the screen protectors and chargers are advised that they have support of 10%, and a confidence level of 85%. The subsequent further sequence analysis revealed that 4 percent customers who bought smartphone also bought chargers thereafter headphones reveal an appropriate sequence. The proposed two paradigms static (association rules) and dynamic (sequential patterns) were tested for validation and the results for Prec = 82% and Recall = 85% signifies that the proposed model will prove efficient and accurate and hence can be used for predicting patterns. Together, these findings will enable the e-commerce platform providers to enhance and/or optimise channel explicit Eric & Baumeister (2011) approach, delivery mechanism and/or recommendation system of their customers as well as tailor their stocks according to the flow of customer movement. This work highlighted the need for the combined approach of association and sequence mining analysis to enhance knowledge regarding the consumer behavior and offers a feasible source for ecommerce platforms to enhance customer experience. This approach can be enriched in future work and adjusted further to obtain better reactions on current changes in behavior of consumers by applying real-time data streaming. The above research framework is helpful for both business and consumers in digital marketplace as it provides right time to market products and services using data which is consistent with consumers’ actual behavior.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Wearable Sensors for Continuous Measurement of Vital Signs in Resource-Limited Settings
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Wearable or noninvasive sensors capable of measuring vital signs continuously can help narrow the resource gap in rarefied environments. The challenge for adoption, though, is the cost of traditional sensors and, in particular, the need for such infrastructure in these settings. To this end, the rapid development of inexpensive wearables allows continuous monitoring of vital signs such as heart rate, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation, and body temperature. The sensors are also lightweight, portable and non-invasive, making them useful for resource-limited settings that have limited access to medical technologies. Utilizing high-tech components like wireless communication and digital signal processing, the sensors provide fast, continuous, real-time monitoring of vital signs. They are easily operated and require little training. These sensors can wirelessly send the gathered data to smartphones or tablets, enabling healthcare workers to monitor patients remotely in real-time. This helps early identification of any unusual readings, allowing timely intervention. These low-cost, noninvasive sensors can compel a paradigm shift in healthcare delivery for resource-constrained settings. Their ability to monitor vital signs 24/7 without the time and expense of patient visits could save both lives and money at a fraction of the cost offered by traditional sensors. These can help us make an early diagnosis and intervention, thus improving the outcomes of patients. Such sensors may provide a solution for the healthcare disparity gap and achieve low-cost, accessible vital sign monitoring to target individuals who need it most.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Firewalls: Enhancing Network Security with Application-Awareness
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: As modern alternatives to traditional firewalls, next-generation firewalls are an essential part of advanced network security, providing increased protection against advanced threats over a conventional firewall with the functionality to identify and control specific applications and traffic on the network. Traditional firewalls are packet-inspecting, port and protocol-centric devices that may miss or allow application-level attacks disguised as normal application traffic. In contrast, NGFWs are application-aware, meaning they know their unique signatures and can discriminate between various applications on the same port. This enables prepaid, more granular policy enforcement and protection against multiple threats, including malware, data breaches and unauthorized access. NGFWs provide application awareness and include intrusion prevention, malware detection, and deep packet inspection, which mean you get a multilayered defense against multiple types of attacks. HARs/HEAs also include central management and reporting features, allowing network administrators to monitor, analyze and quickly respond to potential threats. NGFWs are never static and evolve with the latest pointers in emerging threat vectors. They also offer advanced features like sandboxing and threat intelligence integration built into NGFW modules.

articleTitle: Advancing Brain-Computer Interfaces: A Deep Learning Approach for Enhanced Neural Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Brain-to-computer interfaces (BCIs) are a developing technology that has led to a straight link among the human brain and various systems. The complexity and lack of predictability of brain signals make the development of a trustworthy, accurate BCI system. In this study, we look into how advanced deep learning approaches like Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Graph Isomorphism Networks (GIN), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) can be used to improve neural signal processing performance in BCI. LSTM and GRU are good at discovering the temporally related EEG sequences, while CNNs extract the spatial feature of raw EEG data very well. We model and analyze graph-structured data from functional brain networks using GIN, revealing insights into spatial dynamics and inter-channel connections. Both graph-based and spatiotemporal features are integrated as proposed in the framework, and a deep learning architecture is constructed for signal decoding and classification that allows for a higher signal decoding and classification accuracy. Our experimental results on publicly available EEG datasets demonstrate that this approach outperforms standalone deep learning models and traditional machine learning approaches. It designs its solutions to attain higher accuracy, robustness, and the ability to generalize across various BCI tasks, including cognitive state recognition and motor imagery classification. The result indicates that our model LSTM is 96.92%, CNN is 95.95%, GRU is 95.40%, and GIN is 88.68%. Finally, this study demonstrates how advanced deep learning techniques can address the current limitations of BCI systems, opening the door for more reliable and successful real-world applications.

articleTitle: Real-Time Environmental Monitoring and Control Using Cyber-Physical Systems: A Case Study in Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Due to its nature, real-time environmental monitoring and control is an indispensable part of modern agriculture. At its core, it is the ongoing collection, analysis, and application of ecological data to improve crop yields while conserving resources and minimizing expenditures. This article proposes that cyber-physical systems are an effective organization that provides a building structure where real-time monitoring and control can be provided across different processes within agriculture. Here, we report on a detailed case study of the application of CPS as discussed for environmental monitoring and control in agriculture. This paper reviews the dominant components of CPS sensors, actuators, and communication systems and data analytics. Together, these elements help us to gather real-time data on critical environmental variables like temperature, humidity, soil moisture and nutrient levels. The algorithm analyzes the data and provides farmers with insights. With the help of CPS, farmers can automate and remotely monitor essential processes like watering, fertilization, pest control, etc., increasing efficiency while decreasing labor costs. Another benefit of CPS is that it makes accurate decisions in a timely manner using real-time data, which can yield better crops and be more effective in resource utilization.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Talent Acquisition and Employee Retention Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Human resources (HR) procedures have been drastically altered by artificial intelligence (AI) fast expansion, particularly in the areas of talent acquisition and employee retention. Though they are working hard to develop successful recruitment plans and keep good retention rates, organizations nonetheless struggle with issues including prejudices in decision-making and too high personnel turnover. Among other possible responses, artificial intelligence (AI) might automate administrative chores, offer predictive insights on employee happiness and attrition issues, and simplify candidate screening. In order to improve recruitment and retention rates, this article examines how artificial intelligence (AI) might be included into human resource (HR) systems utilizing predictive models and machine learning techniques. Python using TensorFlow and scikit-learn tools allowed us to create and assess a hybrid artificial intelligence framework. This framework helped to organize data on employee satisfaction and recruiting from many companies. The first tests have demonstrated that the framework precisely projects possible resignations with a 91% accuracy rate and increases recruitment efficiency by 28%. Comparisons with more conventional approaches draw attention to the more exact and affordable HR models augmented with artificial intelligence have been improved with. The significant findings imply that by lowering bias, improving decision-making, and motivating long-term employee involvement, artificial intelligence could support human resource teams. These findings reveal how artificial intelligence could modify human resource practices to attain better performance.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Interference Management in Dense Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: System mastering strategies have been extensively utilized in numerous programs to improve the overall performance of complex systems, and they have these days received widespread attention in wireless networks. One vicinity-specific hobby is in interference control in dense Wi-Fi networks, where the growing wide variety of gadgets and high record demands has resulted in extreme interference issues. Conventional strategies, which include power control and aid allocation, have constrained effectiveness in such situations, calling for a superior strategy. System mastering offers a promising solution that utilizes statistics-driven procedures to manage interference in dense networks. With the aid of studying historic network records and continuously adapting to changing environments, machine learning algorithms could make extra efficient and correct selections in handling interference as compared to conventional strategies. Those algorithms can also take care of the complexity of dense networks and remember more than one element, which includes consumer places, network topology, and traffic styles. Several system-studying strategies, along with reinforcement studying and deep learning, have been implemented for interference control in dense networks. These strategies have shown progress in minimizing interference and growing typical network capability. Gadget studying can also permit proactive interference management by predicting destiny network situations and taking preemptive actions to avoid ability interference. Device learning strategies display first-rate potential in addressing the demanding situations of interference in dense wireless networks. They are able to beautify network performance and efficiency while lowering the need for human intervention, making them a promising solution for the constantly evolving Wi-Fi landscape.

articleTitle: A Study on Work-Life Balance Among Nurses in Trivandrum District
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: Nurses have to strike a good balance between their personal and professional life considering the rig of their work. Typical difficulties for nurses in striking a good balance between their personal and professional life are irregular work schedules, emotional stress, and lack of time for personal responsibilities. This mismatch might affect their general well-being, mental health, and job satisfaction as well. Methodology: One must first completely grasp these challenges before one can provide efficient support to nurses in the Trivandrum district, whose healthcare systems are growing. With an eye towards especially the effect of their professional obligations on their personal life, this study examines the work-life balance of Trivandrum nurses. We applied a mixed-methods approach, obtaining quantitative data by means of well crafted questionnaires and qualitative insights by means of interviews. Findings: 150 nurses from public and private hospitals together answered the survey. Among many important factors considered were working hours, degrees of emotional tiredness, time spent with family, and self-reported job satisfaction. SPSS enabled statistical analysis to find obvious trends and relationships. Based on the findings, 68 percent of nurses claimed to have moderate to high degrees of work-life imbalance. Results: Of those nurses, 42 percent attributed long working hours and 37 percent pointed the finger on irregular shifts. About fifty-five percent of the respondents said they needed organisational support and more flexible work schedules. With a mean score of 3.8/5, those working for public universities reported a rather better balance than those working for private hospitals; their mean score was 3. Work-life imbalance and emotional tiredness show a significant correlation (r=0.72), which underlines the need of therapies including counselling and flexible schedule.

articleTitle: Game Theory Based Spectrum Sharing Techniques for Cognitive Radio Networks with Multiple Primary Users
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The recreation concept has been delivered in cognitive radio networks (CRNs) as an effective approach for spectrum sharing amongst more than one number one user (PUs). This method permits secondary customers (SUs) to utilize the unused spectrum sources of the PUs while minimizing interference to their primary transmissions. This is especially important in CRNs, where the constrained availability of spectrum assets is a first-rate assignment. In this paper, we advocate sport idea-primarily based spectrum sharing techniques for CRNs with multiple PUs. We formulate the problem as a non-cooperative game wherein SUs choose their transmission strategies to maximize their utilities while thinking about the restrictions imposed by the PUs. The proposed techniques consist of coalitional sport-based total power control, software-primarily based negotiation, and cooperative spectrum sharing through aspect charge. Simulation outcomes display that these strategies can achieve better spectrum utilization and equity among SUs compared to standard methods while also ensuring minimum interference to the PUs.

articleTitle: The Threat Landscape of Ransomware in Critical Infrastructure: An Optimization Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Ransom ware, a malicious software program, has become a main threat to essential infrastructure systems, including power, transportation, and healthcare systems. This kind of cyber-attack is designed to block access to important records or devices until a ransom is paid, doubtlessly inflicting sizeable disruptions to critical offerings. As an increasing number of industries become reliant on technology, the threat of ransom ware in vital infrastructure has expanded. We provide an optimization angle at the danger panorama of ransom ware in critical infrastructure. We first examine the factors that contribute to the vulnerability of important infrastructure structures to ransom ware assaults. These consist of old technology, lack of education and cognizance, and insufficient backup and healing systems. We then discover the ability effects of a successful ransom ware attack on essential infrastructure, including manufacturing delays, service outages, and economic losses. We also examine different optimization techniques for stopping, mitigating, and responding to ransom ware attacks in critical infrastructure. These encompass risk-based total strategies, intrusion detection and prevention structures, and cyber coverage. We observe the function of government guidelines and policies in addressing the risk of ransom ware in critical infrastructure. Our findings provide insights for decision-makers in essential infrastructure industries to optimize their techniques and investments in stopping and responding to ransom ware attacks. By considering the optimization angle, essential infrastructure structures can better guard against the ever-evolving chance panorama of ransom ware.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Blockchain-Based Cryptographic Framework for Network Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Blockchain technology is increasingly developing breakthroughs in secure and decentralized data storage. More recently, it has also garnered interest as a possible solution for network security. In particular, this paper conducts an indepth analysis of a network security cryptographic framework using Blockchain. The framework proposed again adopts the principles of blockchain technology, such as decentralization, immutability and consensus, to build a secure data environment for the network. It uses various cryptographic methods, digital signatures and Encryption and hash functions, to guarantee integrity, confidentiality, and authentication. The framework uses smart contracts to automatically execute security checks that can be enforced with predefined and approved methods. In this analysis, we aim to investigate the proposed scheme's effectiveness, scalability, and practicability in typical network security applications. It will also cover the challenges and future research directions in applying this framework in practical scenarios. This analysis will form the basis for a strong cryptographic system on the Blockchain to provide security reinforcement in networks.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Talent Acquisition in Human Resources with Advanced Deep Learning-Based Resume Screening and Candidate Matching Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In general, this paper outlines a research agenda to transform the approach to talent management in HR using deep learning strategies for enhanced resume analysis and candidate matching. The above work proposed and developed a system that exploits the most advanced tools of natural language processing, and recent advances in neural networks to correctly parse resumes and the candidates to jobs descriptions. The system deals with the issues of unstructured resume data, the efficient extraction of the required data, and assessment of the candidate on his/her fitness in the given company in terms of his/her technical competencies and compatibility with the company's work culture. Substantial real life data analysis presented in the paper proves high efficiency and equity of the applications. This research also incorporates the ethical questions as well as the ways of dealing with data privacy regulations and the biases in the historical data by applying the explainable AI methods. A questionnaire to the users of the system, which are the HR professionals further verifies the real-world application and usability of the system based on concepts such as ease of use, precision and time economy. In conclusion, the study adds knowledge to the process of establishing ethical and optimal AI implementations in the field of HRM and results in the improvement of talent recruitment strategies and practices promoting fair hiring decisions.

articleTitle: Hydrocephalus Classification From MRI Using Learning Vector Quantization-Based Factorization Machine Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: The brain collecting cerebrospinal fluid defines the neurological condition known as hydrocephalus. Appropriate diagnosis of the condition for the patients determines how well hydrocephalus is treated. Although MRI scans are widely used in diagnosis, hand classification can be time-consuming and prone to errors. A method able to regularly and automatically classify hydrocephalus depending on MRI scans is absolutely necessary to improve clinical decision-making responsibilities. Conventional machine learning techniques find it sometimes difficult to detect the intricate patterns in MRI data because of its great dimensionality. The current solutions need feature engineering, which can be time-consuming and prone to errors brought about by human involvement. To thus increase the accuracy of classification, one must use a sophisticated approach combining deep learning and machine learning techniques. Proposed Methodology: This work intends to propose a hybrid model comprising deep learning, Learning Vector Quantisation (LVQ), and factorisation machines (FM). Whereas the LVQ is used for feature learning, the FM captures high-order interactions discovered in MRI features helps to improve model performance. Findings: The model was taught to identify hydrocephalus cases from a dataset including MRI scans. Reaching a 92.5% classification accuracy, the proposed model uses a sensitivity of 91.2% and a specificity of 94.1%. With its improved performance, the model's accuracy, 6% higher than that of conventional machine learning techniques, shown its capacity to effectively identify hydrocephalus from MRI scans.

articleTitle: Enabling Interoperability in Heterogeneous IoT Networks through Standardization Protocols
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The Internet of Things is a tremendous technology paradigm due to its ability to help perform intercommunication and coordination across different devices and systems. But nowadays, as the number of IoT devices and applications escalates, one of the key challenges is interoperability between heterogeneous IoT networks different devices and delivery systems that need to communicate and exchange data. This definition necessitates a protocol for standardization, be it implicit or explicit. Standardization protocols would lead to a corresponding need for seamless interoperability between heterogeneous IoT networks. This technical abstract proposes a recommendation for addressing this issue. We then discuss how standardization helps to ensure compatibility and smooth interoperation among IoT devices and systems. We also talk about the various standardization protocols in the marketplace, including MQTT, CoAP and OPC UA, and their compatibility with different IoT devices and platforms. We also discuss the challenges and limitations of deploying standardization protocols for heterogeneous IoT networks that arise due to miscellaneous, non-premium network IO and standards-protocols non-uniformity.

articleTitle: Next Generation Energy Storage Solutions for the Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The automobile industry is shifting closer to electrification; the need for dependable and efficient answers to electricity garages has become increasingly important. The present-day era of batteries, specifically lithium-ion, is attaining its limitations in terms of overall performance, price, and protection. Consequently, the development of next-era power storage answers is crucial to fulfill the growing demands of the enterprise. Subsequent-technology energy garage answers aim to enhance the constraints of present-day batteries by making use of new materials, designs, and technologies. It includes stable-state batteries, which use strong electrolytes as opposed to liquid ones, presenting better electricity density and improved protection. Other solutions include metallic-air batteries that use air as the cathode, promising extensively higher power densities. There are also traits in power garage devices that use ultra-capacitors, promising faster-charging instances and longer lifetimes. Those improvements are only some of the most effective advantages for the automobile enterprise, but they also have potential for packages in other regions, including renewable power storage. However, there are nevertheless challenges to conquer, including improving production procedures to reduce charges and increasing the durability and reliability of these next-technology solutions.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Smart Agriculture: Real-Time Crop Monitoring and Yield Prediction for Sustainable Farming
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In this case Internet of Things (IoT) based smart farming is a revolution sample for modernization of agriculture and made them more sustainable. This research aims at proposing a smart agriculture system that incorporates the IoT in monitoring crops cereals in their real-time yield prediction. Instead, through the network of sensors, cameras, and drones, the system continuously acquires data on soil moisture, temperature, light intensity, and the like. The above data is analyzed through machine learning models in a bid to forecast crop health, rates of growth, and more elaborately, yields. The system also lets farmers keep abreast of their fields, and act quickly if there are unfavorable conditions like pest or diseases, or water constraints. The analyses made concerning irrigation, fertilizer application and pest control are also informed by the predictive analytics model, adopting resource efficiency for maximum returns. The objective of this study will be to provide a proof of concept that IoT enabled solutions can be implemented and will have a positive impact on productivity and sustainability of agriculture. The IoT system gives the farmers timely requirements and the capability of future prognosis, thus enhancing the farming's efficiency in terms of crop production through precision farming. Apart from the issue of food insecurity this approach also takes care of the destruction of the environment by practices such as large scale monoculture farming by directing the society to the right course to a sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Skin Lesion Classification Using EfficientNet-B7 and Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Melanoma skin cancer is a major global health problem, and this makes early diagnosis an essential element in treatment. In this research work, a multi class skin lesion classification model based on EfficientNet-B7 along with ensemble approaches is developed. The objective is to improve the predictive power for skin lesion detection systems, while incorporating the best aspects of deep learning techniques as well as ensemble learning. In order to extract a set of representative features, EfficientNet-B7 is applied for the CNN model as the feature extraction technique, and ensemble learning is a powerful technique which combines multiple models to attain higher accuracy, prevent overfitting, and heave more numbers of classes. The advantage of the proposed methodology is illustrated by the results of experiments with a large skin lesion database showing better diagnostic accuracy as compared to individual models and current literature approaches. The performance of the proposed ensemble model for lesion type classification is summarized in accuracy, precision, and recall, and F1-score with an overall of 94.8%. It is shown that the ensemble technique improves the melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and benign classification remarkably. The conclusion of this research will utilize potential solution for the automated detection and diagnosis of skin lesions this paper thus offer a reliable equipment to clinicians, in preventing and managing skin lesions through early detection. Possible subsequent work may include enhancingletalizing onto more modalities for improved performance of the system and their relevance for clinical practice.

articleTitle: Consumer Behavior Trends - The Influence of Social Media Marketing on Brand Loyalty Among Millennials
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: For decades, who make up a significant share of the internet population, social media marketing has changed the interaction between consumers and brands. Fast spread of platforms including Instagram, TikHub, and Facebook has resulted in the creation of new channels by which companies may interact with customers, therefore increasing the link of connection and loyalty. Examining one of the most important questions is how loyalty of this particular group is affected by social media efforts. Objectives: This work used machine learning models to quantify, utilising several social media marketing components including engagement rate and content kind, the effect on brand loyalty. A survey-based quantitative analysis mixed with data from social media interactions allowed to reach the quantification. Findings: Companies who used interactive content and influencer relationships had an average increase in consumer loyalty of 28%, based on the data showing a notable association. With a 3.5% standard deviation, the model revealed 82% percent accuracy in predicting the elements influencing brand loyalty. These findings underline the significance of smart social media marketing as a basic component in regards of motivating millennial long-term brand loyalty.

articleTitle: Image Captioning-A Comprehensive Encoder-Decoder Approach on Flickr8K
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This paper proposes a new encoder-decoder frame-work based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for image caption generation. Image captioning, the process of generating descriptive textual content for images, has diverse applications, including accessibility tools for the visually impaired, virtual assistants, social media automation, and satellite imagery analysis in critical domains like defense and disaster management. The proposed model will leverage the power of CNNs for extracting high-level image features and LSTMs for generating semantically coherent captions. Rigorously evaluated on the Flickr8k dataset, the model achieved competitive BLEU scores, showing its efficacy in generating accurate and meaningful descriptions. The methodology integrates advanced preprocessing techniques and efficient training strategies, ensuring robustness and scalability. This re-search focuses on the need to use state-of-the-art machine learning techniques in the solving of real challenges, and some of the potential routes to improving image captioning systems are suggested to include multilingual capabilities and integration with larger datasets. Contributions include a clear explanation of the encoder-decoder approach, detailed metrics for evaluation, and insights into correcting limitations including dataset size and complex scene representation. This work is a step toward further progress in automated image-to-text systems, integrating precision, relevance, and adaptability.

articleTitle: Adaptive Cybersecurity Framework Utilizing Random Forest and SVM for Real-Time Threat Detection in Cloud Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Many cyber threats affect cloud computing environments such as zero day exploits and advanced persistent threats (APTs). In order to solve this problem, we put forward an adaptive cybersecurity model based on Random Forest and Support Vector Machines (SVM) for threat detection in realtime. This position is implemented in the current hybrid model of Random forest, which provides the feature set optimization from the Random forest while the SVM is able to handle the complexity of the data and the features and dimensions thereof. It is thus a system that can learn; the parameters of new threats are identified online hence enhancing new and better results constantly. As demonstrated by experimental data, the proposed framework accomplishes detection accuracy of 98.1%, precision 97.9%, and low false positives of 0.8%. The framework is modular, extendible and elastict, and can deal with large volumes of data in cloud environments, thus appropriate for real-time threat detection. This work advances the available literature on cloud security in an effort to offer a more adaptive and continuous method for countering cyber threats.

articleTitle: Designing Energy-Efficient Embedded Systems with CNNs for Real-Time Control in Autonomous Robotics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This research proposes an energy-aware paradigm for the implementation of deep learning using CNN for real-time control in autonomous robotics for embedded systems. The overall power efficiency of the proposed system is achieved through efficient control of power consumption, latency, and runtime while has minor degradation in terms of accuracy through a number of approaches including model pruning, quantization, and adaptive CNN scaling. Studies show that power consumption has been cut down to as low as 47.3% thereby making the optimized system's power consumption in obstacle avoidance tasks as low as 2.8 W, the base system consuming up to 5.0 W power The delay was also lowered to 47.1% in key tasks from 20 ms, thus ensuring more immediate decisions in real time activities. Also, the system up time was enhanced by 40% to perform operations including object identification and sensors integration. Accuracy stayed over 92% in all tasks; the fully optimized CNN design was 0.6% less accurate than an ideal 95.0%, with a 92.4% score. These results endorse that much energy savings and performance improvement are realizable whilst incurring moderate costs on the precision of RTAS, which makes this approach perfect for battery operated, constraint embedded systems in ‘smart’ robotics.

articleTitle: Impact of Organisational Agility on Change Management with the Mediating Effect of Technological Advancement in its Sector
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: Effective change management in the fast-paced information technology industry of today depends quite definitely on organisational agility. With an eye towards the mediator-that is, technological development-this study intends to examine the relationships between agility and change management strategies. Methodology: Although agility is obviously crucial, its direct impact on change management is still unknown, particularly in relation to the fast increase of technological capacities. We asked three hundred information technology professionals working for different companies a quantitative survey. Findings: Structural equation modelling (SEM) was used in data analysis. Change management and organisational agility have a positive correlation, according to the study (β = 0.45, p = 0.01). Moreover, technological development turned out to be a main mediator in this relationship (mediating effect = 0.32). When compared to their less agile counterparts, companies with high degrees of agility and advanced technologies observed a 25% increase in the number of successful change projects.

articleTitle: IoT and Sensor-based Water Quality Monitoring for Sustainable Management of Water Resources
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: we are now moving into an era where the Iota and sensor-based technologies can monitor many parameters, including water quality. Since fresh, potable water is becoming increasingly scarce in many parts of the globe, maintaining a clean and sustainable source for consumption remains one of our biggest challenges today. This challenge can be addressed by leveraging IoT and sensor-based systems that accumulate data from several devices plus study it toward make insight designed meant for better executive. Most available IoT and sensor-based water quality monitoring systems use a network of devices, generally called sensors or data loggers that are connected to take in the multiple variables related to parameters like pH levels, dissolved oxygen placeholders d, and pollutants. This data is subsequently integrated with scientific algorithms and machine learning, which helps to determine water quality fluctuations in near real-time. These systems can be combined with geographic information systems, illuminating the data and making it mappable so that problem areas will likely emerge. IoT and sensor-based water quality monitoring are advantageous against conventional methods in terms of better accuracy, increased efficiency, cost-effectiveness to monitor long term, and the ability to demonstrate effective real-time information about water fettle. Information like this can be critical for managing water resources, as it can identify potential problems such as contamination or water running out. It optimizes these technologies to monitor remote locations, decreasing human labor requirements and enabling real-time decision-making in sustainable water resource management.

articleTitle: Movie Recommendation System Using Hybrid Based Method
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The rise of digital platforms has increased user engagement and satisfaction through personalized recommendation systems. The research paper presents a hybrid approach to movie recommendation, which uses content-based filtering and collaborative filtering techniques to mitigate the cold start problem, data sparsity, and scalability issues. The proposed system will utilize methodologies from machine learning, such as cosine similarity and vectorization, and the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm, for recommending movies based on their precise and personalized values. The dataset TMDB5000 will then be used for two datasets involving movie features, cast, and crew information while preprocessing techniques in cleaning, feature extraction, and merging are undertaken to ensure robust foundation for the model building. The hybrid model uses the bag-of-words technique to vectorize and compute cosine similarity to determine movies' relationships in a multidimensional space. The KNN algorithm then refines the collaborative filtering process by the clustering of user preferences and makes recommendations using nearest-neighbor analysis. Our current approach overcomes these weaknesses by combining both content-based and collaborative methods, resulting in a system which handles diverse user preferences while maintaining high recommendation accuracy. As the evaluation of precision, recall, F1-score, and mean squared errors further validates that this system performance is good and also scalable and efficient for processing large datasets for which it explains some practical aspects related to implementation in real time. The future work includes deep learning models like neural collaborative filtering to further improve semantic understanding and recommendation accuracy. This paper addresses the current system's limitations by proposing a novel, efficient, and user-centric hybrid approach, which can be extended to other domains, such as e-commerce, music, and book recommendations.

articleTitle: The Impact of Remote Work on Employee Engagement and Organizational Culture in the Post-Pandemic Computational Perspective
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 epidemic has hastened the move to remote work, therefore altering corporate interactions with employees and influencing their protection of their culture. Concurrent with this change has been issues with communication, teamwork, and preserving a common organizational identity. The transition has generated some challenges even if it has increased skill pool and adaptability. Motivation: The purpose of this study is to evaluate, in the years following an outbreak, the effects of working remotely on employee engagement and the corporate culture. Findings: Based on the findings of quantitative research, 54<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of respondents have indicated a decline in natural workplace cooperation while 68% have stated continuous productivity using a range of research approaches including qualitative interviews with human resource managers from fifty companies spanning medium to big in size and surveys with 500 remote workers. Results: While working remotely helps to achieve a work-life balance, the results reveal that it can be bad for the nonverbal signals needed for the cohesiveness and reliability of a team. To properly close these divisions, a structure incorporating hybrid models and regular virtual team-building activities has been developed. This indepth research seeks to highlight the complex effects of working remotely and provide strategic insights for organizational leaders so enabling more employee involvement while maintaining their culture.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Meets Traditional Machine Learning: CNN-SVM Hybrid Models for Parkinson's Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that needs early and accurate diagnosis for good management. Our approach in this study is to have a hybrid diagnostic framework which uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for the feature extraction, and Support Vector Machines (SVMs) for the classification. By leveraging on the complementary strengths of the above-mentioned approaches, the model reports improved performance in detection of PD by using medical imaging data. We evaluated proposed CNN-SVM hybrid model on a dataset consist of 5,000 MRI images (2,500 with PD cases and 2,500 with healthy control) with achieved accuracy of 94.8%, sensitivity of 93.7%, and specificity of 95.5%. These results demonstrate a significant improvement over baseline methods, including standalone CNNs (accuracy: 91. The performance of the proposed methods is experimentally demonstrated to be better than SVMs with handcrafted features (accuracy: 84.5%, sensitivity: 83.2%, specificity: 85.0%) and even SVMs using Fisher vectors (accuracy: 81.4%, sensitivity: 86.1%, specificity: 81.1%) for certain classes (e.g. 2%, sensitivity: 89.5%, specificity: 92.3%). The class separability of the hybrid model was excellent, with an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC−ROC) of 0.96. These findings were further confirmed under confusion matrix analysis with 2,343 true positives and 2,388 true negatives and with only 157 false negatives (sensitivity: 0.017%) and 112 false positives (specificity: 0.970%). The model demonstrated generalizability by the convergence of training and validation curves throughout 50 epochs with a final loss of 0.06 and validation error stabilizing at 0.04. The CNN-SVM hybrid model also can demonstrate the ability to become a reliable diagnostic tool for PD detection, with robust classification performance and few errors. Multi-modal data integration and scalability for use over a broader range of clinical applications is the subject of future work.

articleTitle: Optimizing Logistics in E-Commerce Using Deep Random Forest for Enhanced User Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Operational efficiency is one of the most important factors affecting customer satisfaction directly in e-commerce. Still, constant addressing of timely delivery, path simplification, and reduction of delays remains challenging problems. Deep Random Forest (DRF) is a new approach presented in this work to examine and forecast significant logistics metrics including delivery times and satisfaction scores. Development of this approach targeted to solve these issues. The model makes use of e-commerce past performance including order volumes, customer comments, and delivery times. Findings: The suggested approach achieves 10% increase in user satisfaction, 12% cost reduction, and 15% faster delivery times than baseline methods. This is accomplished by means of DRF, applied to examine trends and carry out predictive modifications. Results and Methodology: These results outperform those of the benchmarks established by Gradient Boosting and XGBoost, which displayed respective rises in satisfaction of 9% and 8%. Apart from improving the quality of service, the use of DRF not only strengthened user loyalty but also contributed to improve the transportation efficiency. This approach exposes the transforming opportunities of artificial intelligence in logistics management for e-commerce systems. This approach guarantees operations with a customer-centric concentration benefiting from measurable advantages.

articleTitle: Throughput Maximization in Wireless Powered Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: One promising solution for energy-constrained wireless devices is wireless-powered communication networks (WPCNs), where mobile users harvest energy from the dedicated transmitters, which power the information transmission and do not need to rely on limited-life batteries. Nevertheless, the major issue in WPCNs lies in how to achieve high throughput, and yet energy constraint-compliant devices need to be considered. Summary: This paper surveys throughput maximization in WPCNs. One way to enhance the throughput of WPCNs is to perform resource allocation by which available energy and communication resources are jointly allocated among devices. The value of harvesting energy compared to transmitting data will be the same through different techniques like power splitting and time sharing. The third major problem of WPCNs for harvesting maximum throughput is energy transmission, which uses the energy sources through their power levels to ensure optimal scheduling order to supply power. Other advanced techniques like dynamic power control and channel estimation are implemented to optimize the overall system throughput and obtain higher energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Optimized User Scheduling for Full-Duplex Communications in Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Full duplex communication allows a user to transmit and receive data at the same time, and it has been seen as a promising technique to increase the efficiency and throughput of wireless networks. This, in turn, causes new kinds of problems like self-interference and intra-post interference, causing unfairness to other users. In this paper, we present an optimized user scheduling method for full-duplex communications in wireless networks to address these issues and further improve system throughputs. The schematic of our schedule adjusts the time and frequency for flexibility to obtain suitable resource appointments along with channel conditions and user traffic demand. We also conduct simulations to show that the proposed scheme significantly improves system throughput and fairness over existing scheduling schemes. The proposed scheme will also decrease the self-interference level and enhance the robustness of interference to neighboring networks. The main takeaway from our scheme is to realize the full potential of FD communication in wireless networks, hence providing a more reliable and efficient network for users.

articleTitle: The Role of Flexible Batteries in Enabling Electric Vehicle Adoption
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Flexible batteries, also known as thin-movie batteries, have emerged as a promising technology in the race toward the giant adoption of electrical automobiles (EVs). These batteries provide several blessings over conventional lithium-ion batteries, which currently electricity most EVs, including decreased weight, advanced safety, and better electricity garage capability. One of the foremost demanding situations dealing with EV adoption is the restrained use variety presented through conventional batteries, which require frequent recharging. This has been a major barrier for ability customers, who may have yet to get admission to charging stations or may be deterred by the prolonged charging process. Bendy batteries, with their lightweight and excessive electricity storage potential, can appreciably grow the use of a variety of EVs, making them an extra feasible opportunity for fuel-powered motors. Moreover, bendy batteries may be incorporated into the design of the car, making it possible to create extra aerodynamic and space-green EVs. This allows for greater flexibility in car design and reduces the general value of production. Similarly, as EVs become more extensively used, the call for bendy batteries will grow due to economies of scale and doubtlessly decrease the fee of manufacturing even in addition.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Security Techniques for Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: One of the most important issues for secure communication in the physical layer is developing physical layer security techniques to provide confidentiality and data integrity in wireless communication systems. The properties of the physical channel are used in these methodologies to safeguard communication from eavesdropping and some other security threats. This article presents physical layer security methods that can be implemented in wireless communication systems. Artificial Noise (AN) is one of the most popular techniques. The original signal is combined with a generated by the transmitter in such a way that eavesdroppers cannot easily decode the data. Cooperative Anti-jamming: Yet another strategy for jammer localization is to employ cooperative jamming, where multiple friendly users can add noise signals over the signal in an effort to confuse potential eavesdroppers. In addition, additional technologies such as multi-input multi-output beamforming and transmit power control can further improve the security of wireless communication systems. In this regard, strategies based on game theory have been proposed as a viable alternative to enhancing physical layer security. Viewing the interaction between the transmitter, receiver, and eavesdropper as a game allows us to reveal their optimal strategies and security levels.

articleTitle: Real-Time Fraud Detection in Financial Transactions Using Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Data Mining Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The real-time hybrid model of SVM and data mining, developed in this paper aims at detecting fraudulent financial transaction. All these have been developed in Python with Python Scikit-learn to adopt the SVM algorithm, the Pandas for data processing, and Seaborn and Matplotlib for deploying the results. Apache Spark and hence Spark SQL was used to ensure that the framework that handles the transactions data is highly scalable in real time. The data taken into account to this investigation are the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection data set which includes 1,119,000 anonymized records of online credit card transactions. The class imbalance is a major problem in this dataset given that there are many more legitimate transactions than there are fraudulent ones. Therefore, in the present context, two stage concept was employed in the present study which include data preprocessing, feature extraction and integration of svm with clustering and anomaly detection for developing a system for recognition of not only the conventional and emerging frauds. The proposed hybrid model once again looks great with accuracy of 95.2 % of correct answers, a precise coefficient of 91.6 %, and recall coefficient of 90.7 % of true positive; this result is much higher from individual SVM or data mining models. Realtime performance analysis showed that average latency to be 100ms and throughput in terms of number of transaction per second as 800, which specifies that this model is effective for use in intensive traffic loads. Consequently, this work provides a feasible approach to conducting real-time fraud detection with potential for desirable scalability and practical recommendations for developing this aspect of FS security.

articleTitle: Hybridizing a Geothermal Power Plant with Solar Thermal Collectors: A Techno-Economic Feasibility Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Electricity generation with geothermal energy is a mature technology, but the utilization potential has limits concerning resource availability and investment costs. Mixing solar thermal collectors with geothermal is a potential solution to a GEO plant's efficiency and economics. This study analyzes the techno-economic potential of a geothermal power plant with solar thermal collectors' adjunct to it. It features a hybrid plant design that uses the heat from solar thermal collectors to boost the temperature of the geothermal fluid before entering the power plant. A techno-economic analysis assessed the performance and costs of this hybrid system. A hybrid geothermal-solar plant produced 7% more power output than a stand-alone geothermal plant, leadingto an LCOE reduction between 0-10%. we conducted a study focusing on iridization that can be allowed in varied geothermal settings but on and on assessing the cost for different plant capacities. It was found that hybridizing geothermal plants with solar thermal collectors is a very attractive and technically feasible option to increase the efficiency of geothermal power generation under reasonable economic conditions. This technology can pave the way for the possible increment in energy production, lower LCOE, and mainstreaming of renewable energy in the power sector.

articleTitle: Object Detection in Autonomous Driving Systems Using YOLOv5 and Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This paper describes an enhanced approach to perform object detection and tracking for the use of autonomous driving systems by using YOLOv5 model for the detection process, and Kalman filtering for tracking process. The objective is to overcome the difficult tasks of identifying and determining the position of several objects in the context of rapidly changing and diverse conditions that define urban roads, highways, parking lots and in adverse meteorological conditions. For object detection, the relatively accurate and fast YOLOv5 is applied, and for object tracking, we select Kalman filtering based on its stability in cases of occlusions or other changes between frames. The system is tested on several datasets including the urban, highway, parking lot, and adverse weather conditions and measures such as precision rate, recall rate, F1 rate and MOTA, and computational time are used to measure the performance of the algorithm. The findings show that the presented approach gains a high detection rate, consistent object tracking, and sufficiently fast processing, which can be effective for self-driven vehicles. Nevertheless, it has a slightly poor performance in low visibility complicated traffic condition, which is common in real-world application. [This work demonstrates how YOLOv5 and Kalman filtering can be used in autonomous driving and notes that such an approach provides a stable method for object detection and tracking in various conditions for autonomous driving]. In future related improvements, the performance of the developed system will be optimized for operation at even more severe conditions.

articleTitle: Big Data-Driven Customer Experience in E-Commerce: Personalizing User Journeys with Advanced Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In the dynamic nature of business especially in e-commerce, the management of customers has greatly been made to be a cardinal focus of any organization. This paper aims to analyse and discuss applications of big data and customer big data experience to improve the overall customer journey. Application of modern technologies including machine learning, deep learning, and processing real-time data is in the scope of the proposed methodology, which contains a full set of stages including data collection, preprocessing and feature engineering, as well as recommendation generation at the personal level. Neural collaborative filtering (NCF) improved performance results, and the precision and recall rates are greater than 93% suggesting that these methods can better capture complex patterns of user behavior. Real-time personalization also brought sustainable benefits regarding the most important metrics: a 50% increase in average session duration, a 73.5% increase in conversion, and a 38.2% decrease in the cart abandonment rate. Strong customer privacy protection measures were in place to address legal requirements including GDPR, and algorithm ethicality, specifically in bias in personalization guarantee. The results highlight the innovativeness of big data approach in designing positive buying experiences bye-commerce firms. This research offers recommendations for organizations that want to use advanced analytics for digital business innovations based on customer value, which sets the basis for future developments in the realm of personalized electronic commerce.

articleTitle: Radio Resource Management for Hybrid Satellite-Terrestrial Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Hybrid satellite-terrestrial networks demand proficient coordination of Radio Resource Management (RRM). Together, these networks offer the best of both satellite and terrestrial communicative technologies for fast and widespread connectivity. However, it is a difficult task to manage the limited radio resources involved in this very heterogeneous environment. The main goal of RRM in hybrid satellite-terrestrial networks is to provide efficient resource utilization and quality of service support for different applications. They touch on areas such as interference management, spectrum sharing, handover between satellite links, and offloading to terrestrial networks. In order to make RRM more efficient, the following techniques are used during resource allocation: adaptive modulation and coding (AMC), dynamic scheduling, and power control. Such techniques exploit network topology, propagation conditions, and user location to increase spectral efficiency and reduce interference.

articleTitle: Enhancing Tumor Segmentation in MRI Images Using U-Net Architecture with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Segmentation of tumor in MRI is essential for diagnosing the disease, planning the treatment strategy map, and evaluation of disease progress in neuro-oncology. As a consequence, the accurate segmentation of tumors is still a challenging problem due to the complex morphology of the tumor and the intensity in MRI images. In this work, the segmentation is performed by modifying the U-Net structure, which has been enriched with attention modules to produce better segmentation for tumor regions. The Attention U-Net architecture that has been proposed includes spatial attention as well as channel attention in order to let the network pay attention to the most critical areas of the picture and thereby to distinguish between the tumor and non-tumor lesions. Indeed, new multi-scale attention modules allowing for the processing of tumors of various sizes and shapes are also proposed to ensure the consideration of features at different scales. Evaluation of the proposed model is done using MRI dataset that is publicly available with the results in terms of DSC of 0.92, IoU of 0.84 and F1-Score of 0.89, compared to U-Net and other architectural models based on attention. The explained model outperforms the comparative models in segmentation metrics of a similar type, especially in situations where the borders of the tumor may be unclear. The Attention U-Net also preserves computational effectiveness, which is important for real-time work in clinical practice. This work demonstrates that the attention mechanism is highly beneficial for improving tumor segmentation in MRI, hence presenting a reliable means of promoting a better diagnostic approach and treatment planning.

articleTitle: Detection and Prevention from Deepfake Images Videos Using Increasing Frame Method
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In the digital age, the exchange of confidential data over the internet has become an integral part of daily life. Therefore, verifying the authenticity of communication is essential to prevent non-repudiation by the sender. As we know there is alteration of the data by unauthorized is also possible by attempting the attack on that particular data, like there are many original and fake video are available on the internet. Therefore, we need to check that this video is original or fake. Thus, we need some kind of cryptography technique to protect this kind original video from fake video. Now main thing is that how we can find out that a particular video is original or fake. In this research, we are proposing a method by that we can protect video, or pics from deepfake. Here we are converting the video into a frame of pics than we can used the cryptography algorithm to save this data. As we know that, a pic is a combination of the pixels and every pixel is made by color combination of red green and blue. The range of every color is from zero to 255. Therefore, we are using these color values to protect our pic or video. Know we are using least significant bit of every pixel to check that is any changes in our original data. Now we are applying the secure hash algorithm on these least significant bits and make the hash here, as we know that hash is a unique value for a particular input. So, if any one makes the change in our original pic than this hash value will be change. In this paper we are presenting an algorithm by use of it we can secure our video on public platform.

articleTitle: Advanced Signal Processing For IoT Device Communication In Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This work focuses on intelligent home ventilation systems since they provide a fresh approach to the problem. By using renewable energy sources and cloud-based ANFIS architecture, the approach seeks to lower the energy consumption. The study focuses on the creation of a cloud-based cooling system able to maximize energy economy without sacrificing the degree of comfort inherent in the construction. The most important problem is not enough study has been done on how to include renewable energy sources into house cooling control systems. The described method combines a ANFIS system functioning in the cloud with solar power. This system may change the cooling power output in response to occupancy levels, humidity, and temperature as external factors. Conversely, unlike conventional cooling systems, the results imply that 10% of energy consumption might be cut without sacrificing the degree of comfort inside the structure. It is shown via the ANFIS approach that cooling power can be precisely controlled—a essential ability to maximize the use of ecologically friendly energy sources.

articleTitle: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Colon Cancer: Trends, Challenges and Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has made huge enhancements in colon cancer research through its methods for diagnosis, treatment, and custom detection of one of the most common and fatal cancers suffered globally. Through AI deep learning and machine learning methods, tremendous possibilities have been realized in automating, for example, polyp detection in colonoscopy images, cancer classification from histopathological slides, and even predicting disease treatment outcomes. The current direction is towards transfer learning, hybrid model building and AI applications in surgery robots aimed at more accurate diagnosis and treatment procedures. Besides them, however, they have serious disadvantages, access to computer learning systems and datasets are limited, AI models come without explanation, embedding of artificial intelligence into clinical practices becomes troublesome. In future development, emphasize should be on creating databases, explainable ethics AI approaches, building bridges between developers and practitioners in medicine. The objective of the paper is how to incorporate research that has been done in moving colon cancer AI systems into practice, understanding the AI satellites put on colon cancer research.

articleTitle: Stacking-Based Transfer Learning for Optimized Employee Management and Retention in HR Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: For human resources departments trying to ensure organisational stability and lower turnover costs, employee retention is a major challenge. In terms of employee management, traditional approaches often lack the capacity to correctly mix insights from several sources, so limiting the predictive power of these approaches. Methodology: This work proposes a Stacking-Based Transfer Learning (TL) model to support bettering of employee retention policies. This model aggregates domain-specific data and pre-trained models to offer the most exact projections. The approach extracts and combines textual and numerical insights from HR data by means of a hierarchical stacking ensemble of deep learning models, which consists of BERT and ResNet. Tests carried out on a dataset of employee retention easily accessible to the general public reveal the efficiency of the model. Findings and Result: With 92.5%, the suggested method's accuracy exceeded those of other now in use methods including Random Forest (88.3%) and Support Vector Machine (85.7%). Moreover, by 17% over baseline models, the Stacking-based TL model lowers the prediction error linked with employee turnover rates. These findings indicate that HR analytics has great potential to include innovative learning strategies into order to increase employee satisfaction and retention rates respectively.

articleTitle: Automated X-Ray Image Classification for COVID-19 Detection Using DenseNet-121 and SVM
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This paper provides an algorithm to detect COVID-19 from the chest X-Ray images using Two-class classification with DenseNet-121 and Support Vector Machine. For effective identification of patterns suggestive of COVID-19 in the provided X-ray images, we leverage the DenseNet-121 model due to its feature extracting prowess, complemented by the SVM classifier to accurately classify the images between the COVID-19 to non-COVID-19 positive cases. The method delivers a high accuracy, which is more than 93% for accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, which makes it efficient in the COVID-19 quick screening. The Improved DenseNet-121 + SVM was compared with other deep learning models like ResNet50, VGG16, and confirmed that the proposed model has better efficiency in classifying COVID-19 cases. The performance of the model is checked with a five fold cross validation to ensure consistency and reliability on different sets of data not only in terms of performance with the IMDB data but also with the test data. The working paper is relevant to the current research practices in an effort to construct machine diagnostic systems that can be used by practicing healthcare professionals for identifying COVID-19 in the early stages, thus enhancing outcomes in patients' treatment.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Hate Speech Detection and Recognition Utilising Advanced Machine Learning Algorithms and Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Social networking sites have come into demand as a way of sharing ideas and opinions with other people. But unfortunately, people tend to misuse social media to write nasty comments. Victims' lives might be negatively impacted by behaviours that are abusive and humiliating. Social networks give people a great tool to share information on ideas on multiple topics and opinions. However, these platforms are often abused to announce toxic and offensive comments, which eventually negatively affect victims and demographics. This study offers a thorough method for identifying hate speech (HS) on social media by utilising cutting-edge ML algorithms. A publicly available Twitter dataset containing 159,571 tweets classified into six categories, including toxic and identity hatred, was utilised. The methodology comprises data collection, conditioning, and categorisation that employs BiLSTM, which is particularly appropriate for the tasks demanding contextual sensitivity. These operations include symbol removing, stemming and stop-word eliminating, feature extraction using TF-IDF, and using the Bag-of-Words model. For classification of the data between hate and non-hate, the dataset is then split into training and testing datasets and the BiLSTM model used to provide classifications for the text.
