articleTitle: Advanced Learning Platform Integrating AR/VR, AI and Voice Command Technologies for Innovative Educational Experiences
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: This research presents the procedures for designing and implementing a sophisticated learning management system capable of employing augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), artificial intelligence (AI), and voice command technologies to create immersive educational experiences. The developed platform responds to the increasing need for personalized and interactive learning environments that engage students more deeply than traditional methods. With AR and VR, the platform expands the possibilities of visual and experimental learning as students interact with the material not only hands-on but also in a more engaging and three-dimensional way. AI algorithms module the users according to their performance and behaviours, allowing them to change content delivery instantaneously, while voice command technology broadens the audience as there is no contact needed to operate devices. The research investigates the ability of the platform to enhance both physically attending the class and online class activities by providing appropriate feedback, visual performance and video control, respectively. The study's preliminary results show that learning with these technologies improves comprehension and retention while encouraging active participation. This paper also discusses the concepts behind the software's design and the encompassing pedagogical strategies to ensure the successful implementation of the technology in classrooms. Future research directions are presented toward addressing how these technologies improve learning temporal metrics and their application across various scenarios in education.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Driven Diagnosis CNN-LSTM Models for Accurate Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Musculoskeletal disorder knee osteoarthritis (OA) is very prevalent and impacts quality of life demanding accurate grading to inform treatment planning. This study presents a novel deep learning approach based on combination of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks to enhance the accuracy of OA grading. In this, we integrate spatial feature extraction by a ResNet50 backbone and temporal sequence modeling by LSTM which is able to capture both the structural and temporal patterns from radiographic images. Experimental evaluations using the OAI and KAG datasets together with radiographs images classified according to the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) scale are presented. Using the proposed CNN-LSTM model, we achieve accuracy of 92.3%, outperforming previous traditional models (ResNet50 achieves 87.5%; DenseNet-LSTM achieves 89.8%). On the other hand, the model also did better in terms of precision (91.5%), recall (91.8%) and F1-score (91.6%) which shows that it worked well in terms of balance between false positives and false negatives. The robustness of the model was further confirmed via receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis with an area under the curve (AUC) greater than 0.90 across all KL grades. Through varying interpretability, the Grad-CAM visualizations helped validate the results by identifying key join areas of relevance to the OA task. The results show that the proposed CNN-LSTM framework is an accurate, reliable and interpretable solution for automated OA grading. Future work will include improving generalization of the model by augmenting the dataset with multi-modal data from many different patient populations.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Power Wireless Sensor Network for Environmental Monitoring in IoT Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: A wave of IoT devices is being used these days, and keeping the environment stable around them can become challenging. The real-time data collection and analysis of WSN (Wireless Sensor Network) is the only solution that can provide monitoring. In this paper, an ultra-low-power WSN is designed and implemented for monitoring purposes in IoT environments. A full WSN includes low-power environmental sensors, a mesh network of nodes, and a base station functioning as an interface between the Internets. Various sensors monitor ecological parameters like temperature, humidity, and air quality. This data is then sent to the base station over a mesh network, made energy efficient by employing low-power communication protocols. The base station later collates and stores data that is available online for remote access. It is a highly scalable system that supports adding new sensors and nodes as desired. It also integrates security controls to secure the data at rest. The WSN has been deployed successfully in a real-world application, and it is advantageous for sensors to have low power consumption, leading to longer battery life.

articleTitle: Behavior-Based Malware Detection in Enterprise Networks Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Malware attacks have always been regarded as a concern, but today, we should be far more worried about them gaining ground, especially on enterprise networks. Although signature-based techniques have witnessed much success in identifying malware, they can only partially encompass these changing threats. This calls for novel malware detection techniques to identify and neutralize such attacks accurately. In the study, we present a behavior-oriented AI-based malware detection system to identify and prevent malware attacks in enterprise networks. We use artificial intelligence algorithms that analyze the actions of network traffic, applications and devices to identify and classify malicious activity. Large datasets of previous malware behaviors are used to train the AI algorithms to determine new threats, even if the malware has never been seen before. In addition, it can also learn and update the algorithm completely by discovering the latest malware behavior. Our behavior-based detection allows our system to see zero-day attacks and malware variants that standard signature-based detection systems have not seen yet. This significantly improves the security of enterprise networks while minimizing data breaches and financial losses. Our behavior-based malware detection system provides a tailored protection capability against the emerging threat landscape to secure enterprise networks, which is a delegated preventive plan against emergent threats instead of reactive measures. It harnesses the power of AI and adapts to new data to offer a comprehensive layer of protection against malware.

articleTitle: Enhancing Industrial Automation Through IIoT-Enabled Cloud Computing and LSTM for Scalable and Real-Time Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In this thesis, we investigate the combined application of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), cloud computing and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to facilitate advanced industrial automation through the industrial analytics enabled by scalable and real time data processing. IIoT is an industrial approach to generating very large amounts of data from connected industrial devices that can be parsed through cloud computing to yield immediate insights into production processes, equipment health, and operational efficiency. Since this is a time series data, we employ LSTM (A type of recurrent neural network) in this architecture which is able to handle time series data well and is a good fit for predictive maintenance and anomaly detection problems in industrial setting. The proposed system involves three main components: Second, the IoT collection of data from IIoT devices, storage of data in the cloud, and processing of data are stored in the cloud; and finally, real time analysis of data using LSTM models. The LSTM models train on historical datasets containing sensor readings and machine logs, to make accurate equipment failure and process optimization predictions. For large scale data processing we use cloud computing platforms like AWS or Azure to manage where these big databases are located. Evaluation of the system performance is presented in the study with regard to prediction accuracy, latency and a comparison of LSTM with other ML techniques. We can see that that there's strong potential for these technologies to have a powerful impact on industrial automation, downtime, and operational efficiency. Yet, there are still data security and system scalability issues to explore. This research shows that IIoT implants and cloud computing, in conjunction with LSTM, can be designed to transform existing production processes.

articleTitle: A Novel Deep Learning Framework for Diabetes Detection: DiabetesNet
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Due to the steadily rising prevalence of diabetes, early detection is essential for both prevention and effective management. Pima Indians Diabetes dataset has been employed in this study for the verification of proposed approach based on machine learning. Eight clinical characteristics, including age, BMI, insulin concentration, and glucose levels, are included in the dataset and are used to determine if a person has diabetes (1) or not (0). In order to avoid overfitting, we suggest a neural network-based model with three hidden layers that uses Swish activation functions and a Dropout layer for regularization. Dataset is divided into two balanced group called training and testing set. Features are getting normalized using the Min-Max scaling. Early Stopping is used to ensure that the best model parameters are maintained by stopping training as soon as the validation loss stops improving. This maximizes the model's performance. We obtain a classification accuracy of 76% when testing the model on the test set, which offers a strong basis for future model enhancements. F1-score, precision, and recall are used as a performance parameter to evaluate the efficacy of proposed model in classifying patients into two classes viz diabetic or non-diabetic. Although issues like class imbalance and model interpretability still need to be addressed, the results show the promise of deep learning techniques in medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Speech Enhancement for Robust Speech Recognition in Noisy Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: It is a very important problem since voice-controlled devices and speech-to-text transcription are only two examples of how automatic recognition of spoken language in noisy environments may impact our lives. Still, speech recognition systems may only sometimes work effectively in background noise, which can result in errors and misinterpretations. This problem dealt with the deep learning model-based speech enhancement techniques for robust ASR in adverse environments. These methods employ deep learning to learn and deny the noisy speech signals, rendering it a better-suited input for recognition in a typical ASR system. Deep learning-based speech enhancement is a machine-learning system using a huge, loud, clean speech data dataset to train DNN. So, the network is trained to find a mapping from some noisy speech signals to ideally clean versions of these speech sounds by removing its background noise. This spectral representation of speech will now have reduced noise, which the ASR much more easily recognizes. These methods have significantly improved against traditional speech enhancement techniques in demising, eventually improving recognition performance. They can turn in high noise levels and are resilient against acoustics drifts. This makes them well-suited to real-world applications when noise levels can vary.

articleTitle: Explainable AI in Medical Imaging: A Hybrid CNN and Random Forest Framework for Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: A critical disease, a brain tumor must be categorized correctly if treatment and patient management are to be directed. Due to interpretational bias by individuals and errors that are rife in human practice, traditional diagnostic methods sometimes prove wanting. To increase the accuracy of differentiating brain tumors from similar tissues in MR images, this work explores modern computational approaches-particularly CNNs and RFs. This is evidenced by reviewing related literature on MRI-based brain tumor detection, for which deep learning methods are deemed efficient but challenging. The proposed strategy entails preprocessing of the MRI then using CNNs in feature extraction and enhancing performance by the Random Forest classifier. Further, the work uses Explainable Artificial Intelligence (X-AI) approaches, specifically Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), to address the interpretability challenge common in healthcare. Meningiomas yield a 98.5% accuracy, and the other performance parameters calculated that depict a high degree of precision and recall with many tumor types suggest a reasonable classification. This twin objective of maintaining accuracy and interpretability not only enhances the decision-making process of clinicians but also assures trust in deploying AI solutions for producing better patient outcomes in the case of brain tumors.

articleTitle: Efficient Abstraction of Healthcare Data for Real-Time Decision Making Using Logistic Regression and Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Data analytics can help drive decision-making and improve patient outcomes in healthcare. But of course, healthcare data is complex, and the process to access & analyze it can be slow. Here, researchers suggest a way to generalize healthcare data at scale and do so quickly enough for real-time decision support. Logistic regression is used to categorize patient data into various groupings using established standards, which could create a targeted patient population that is at high risk. We then perform linear regression on patients' demographics and medical history to predict their outcomes. This information can help with real-time decisions for patient care. Our method will decrease the time and cost of collecting/analyzing healthcare data for faster decision-making. This is particularly crucial in a rapidly moving healthcare environment where every second counts. Also, logistic and linear regression techniques have been used together to perform a complete data analysis so that the predictions are as accurate as possible. The methodology allows us to effectively abstract healthcare data for healthcare providers' (HCP) real-time decision-making. This process can deliver advances in patient care and efficiencies in effectuating decisions-and it could provide immense benefits across healthcare.

articleTitle: Big Data and Machine Learning for Climate Change Prediction: An Integrated Approach to Environmental Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The integration of big data and machine learning (ML) in climate change prediction offers a transformative approach to environmental monitoring, enabling improved accuracy, scalability, and actionable insights. This study presents an integrated framework that combines the strengths of big data technologies and advanced ML algorithms to address the complexities of climate systems. Diverse datasets from satellites, IoT sensors, and historical records were preprocessed using normalization, feature engineering, and dimensionality reduction techniques to ensure data quality and compatibility. ML models, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and hybrid architectures, were developed to tackle spatial and temporal prediction tasks. The models demonstrated robust performance, with CNNs achieving 93.5% accuracy in deforestation detection and hybrid CNN-RNN models delivering 95% accuracy in cyclone trajectory prediction. Real-time monitoring applications, such as flood risk assessment and air quality forecasting, showcased low latency and scalability, reinforcing the framework's operational viability. Despite these advancements, challenges such as data bias, computational demands, and algorithmic transparency remain significant. To address these, solutions like dataset augmentation, edge computing, and explainable AI are proposed. This research highlights the potential of integrating big data and ML for dynamic and precise climate predictions while emphasizing the need for ethical and equitable deployment of these technologies. By fostering interdisciplinary collaboration and leveraging emerging computational innovations, this study contributes to advancing climate resilience and sustainable environmental management.

articleTitle: Time-Series Analysis of Cancer Progression Using LSTM Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Cancer progression varies; in its simplest definition, it is the growth of abnormal cells anywhere on or within an organism. Time-series cancer data are high dimensional and non-linear, demanding a more advanced approach than traditional statistical tools. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks have become popular for time-series analysis as they can accommodate long-term dependencies well and model complex non-linear patterns. Here, we suggest using LSTM networks in cancer progression data that are often time-dependent and collected for each patient. To accurately identify discriminator signals in the time-series data, we present a stacked LSTM architecture using a deep learning framework generating adversarial examples and feature selection. We have shown that our proposed LSTM approach is superior to common statistical techniques in cancer progression prediction and feature selection. The new cancer progression LSTM network developed a time-series analysis, which has the possibility of being more effective and understandable in monitoring cancer progression for designing offer diagnosis along with treatment compared to the min max AI system.

articleTitle: Work-Life Balance And Its Impact On Job Performance: A Study With Special Reference to Women Police In Chennai City
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: Maintaining a good work-life balance is quite difficult for women in demanding professions like law enforcement. The twin weight of professional obligations and home responsibilities causes stress and burnout among female police officers in Chennai City. Methodology: This paper mostly addresses the challenges faced by female police officers in Chennai as well as the strategies meant to improve their performance at their positions. The study examines for Chennai's female police officers how job performance and work-life balance interact. Split into several ranks, two hundred female police officers from Chennai were handed a preformulated questionnaire. Among the most important things considered are work hours, family responsibilities, job satisfaction, and degrees of perceived stress. The study employs a mixed-method approach combining qualitative insights gained from interviews with quantitative analysis accomplished using regression methodological approaches. Findings: According to the findings, lack of work-life balance causes moderate to high levels of stress for 68 percent of respondents; 72 percent of them claim that such imbalances affect their performance at job. With the stress resulting from an imbalance between job and personal life, the results of the regression analysis show that job performance has a rather negative correlation (R2 = 0.63, p = 0.01). The findings show that right now interventions including flexible work schedules, stress management programs, and institutional support for female officers in order to improve their work-life balance and raise their performance are needed. Among the recommendations are also stressing the need of gender-sensitive policies and building a motivating workplace. This paper seeks to provide a framework for policymaking by means of insightful analysis of the vital influence work-life balance has in determining job performance especially among female police officers.

articleTitle: Adaptive Mutation Strategies in Non-Convex Optimization for Big Data Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: It has been argued that adaptive mutation mechanisms in nonconvex optimization can efficiently handle massive data sets, the curse of big data. Big data is high-dimensional and complex compared to traditional optimization strategies, which can be computationally slow and sub-optimal. Adaptive changes to these parameters in real-time are known as adaptive mutation strategies that adjust them throughout training based on data properties and where they are within the optimization process. This facilitates more accurate and stable solutions, even when the data has noise or uncertainty. In addition, the adaptively of these strategies prevents falling into local optima by exhibiting better global optimization performance. As a result, integrating adaptive mutation strategies into nonconvex optimization for big data processing improves computational efficiency and effectiveness in solving sophisticated, complex problems, thereby making them useful within an era where huge volume exists as well-known with big-data foes.

articleTitle: Enabling Confidentiality in Data Analytics for Outsourced Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Social networks, growing significantly in the past few years, have generated huge amounts of data, which leads to the need for efficient data analytic solutions. On the other hand, social networks contain sensitive data such as personal information and private conversations, which creates privacy and confidentiality issues. A novel solution, Enabling Confidentiality in Data Analytics for Outsourced Social Networks, has been introduced in response. We propose a new framework called ECDAS, which conducts data analytics of outsourced social network data in a privacy-preserving and secure manner without revealing users' information. The main concept is to encrypt the data before outsourcing it to a third-party service provider for analytics while the original sensitive information remains inaccessible. It allows valuable insights to be mined from user data while preserving user's privacy. Additionally, the ECDAS framework provides a mechanism for ensuring secure data sharing and protection to guarantee that only authorized access can be allowed to top the encrypted social network dataset. ECDAS can also scale and become efficient on small-scale and large social networks, making it even more flexible. In summary, ECDAS is a viable solution to ensure confidentiality in the context of data analytics for both outsourced social networks and semi-honest attackers while offering good trade-offs between privacy protections and accurate analytics performance, providing an enhanced overall user experience.

articleTitle: Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) Techniques for 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple gets entry (NOMA) is a promising approach for 5G networks that permits numerous users to percentage the identical time and frequency assets. In contrast to conventional wireless conversation techniques, NOMA permits various customers to get the right of entry to the equal channel simultaneously via the usage of exclusive strength tiers and superposition coding. This results in a greater efficient use of scarce spectrum resources and increases the general capacity for gadgets. NOMA has received interest as an ability solution for the increasing demand of high statistics charges and connectivity in 5G networks. One of the key blessings of NOMA is its capability to aid a massive range of customers with numerous pleasant service requirements. By allocating different strength stages to each user, NOMA can serve each low and excessive records rate user simultaneously, providing an honest and green sharing of sources. Moreover, NOMA permits for higher person scheduling and control, as it could dynamically regulate the energy ranges based on the channel conditions of every person. NOMA can significantly improve the overall performance of Destiny 5G networks by enabling green aid allocation, supporting a large number of customers, and enhancing network capability and consumer revel. It's far predicted that NOMA will play a vital function in the improvement and deployment of 5G networks, in addition to riding the evolution of wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Survey on the Pixel-Based Image Segmentation Techniques with the Intent of Optimization of System Throughput in the Field of Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Semantic segmentation, being one of the Computer Vision approaches, helps in portioning every object in an image, which makes it a good candidate that can be used in various applications like Medical Imaging and Autonomous vehicles. In the Medical field, clear analysis of images like MRI, CT scan, provides the accuracy in identifying the issue and to give proper medications. In the similar way, the pel-based segmentation (semantic segmentation) when used in identifying the objects on roads to ease the driving process requires computations in a precise way and often tend to use neural networks. These networks perform well when the size and amount of data is less but when it comes to training high resolution and larger amounts of data, it results in reduced flexibility of the desired implementation, thereby reducing its efficacy. In this work, the insights of methods and techniques used in the process of semantic segmentation in automation and the medical field is reviewed with the objective of providing a precise summary of techniques that can be used for selecting the best method to achieve best results. The findings of the comparison study shows that the COCO dataset has a large number of images and when used with efficient network architecture with criteria to segment, it can outperform. The contribution of this survey in the field of semantic segmentation outperforms by providing the precise description of deep learning techniques, listing out the complexities and associated techniques to reduce them, and summarizing associated datasets. comparison analysis of techniques to achieve accuracy with less computations.

articleTitle: Challenges and Solutions for Securing Cloud-Based Virtual Private Networks (VPNs)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Cloud-based virtual private networks are becoming common as fewer connections to the company network make them cost-effective and convenient. Nonetheless, increased cyber-attacks and data breaches have made it incredibly difficult for organizations to secure these VPNs. In this technical abstract, we will highlight & describe issues with securing cloud-based VPNs, along with a few ideas for making them secure. In the first rung, there are those weaknesses of cloud-based VPN infrastructure. Since these VPNs are hosted on third-party cloud servers, they are susceptible to DoS and DDoS attacks. Moreover, due to the collaborative/inexpensive nature of cloud servers, they are also vulnerable when it comes to leaking data and getting unauthorized access. The second challenge is that managing the security of so many VPN connections becomes very difficult. Keeping track of all VPN users and their devices and which security protocols are being used becomes cumbersome for organizations, making detecting and responding quickly to a security breach difficult. Organizations should consider implementing multi-factor authentication and strong encryption protocols for their cloud-based VPNs to remedy these complications. Regular vulnerability assessments and penetration tests are also important to identify security risks. Also, a centralized network security management system can ensure more visibility and control of VPN connections.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Full Potential of Battery Energy Storage Systems in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The arena shifts closer to sustainable transportation, electric-powered vehicles (EVs) have emerged as a promising solution to reduce greenhouse gasoline emissions. However, the great adoption of EVs faces numerous challenges, such as confined riding ranges and lengthy charging instances. Battery electricity storage systems were diagnosed as a critical technology to address those barriers and free up the total capacity of EVs. BESS allows for the efficient garage and control of power in EVs, allowing quicker charging instances and extended driving variety. This gadget now not only benefits the vehicle proprietor but also offers grid flexibility and balance by helping smart charging and car-to-grid (V2G) capabilities. BESS additionally has the potential to reduce the strain on the present power grid by moving charging demand to off-peak hours. To completely leverage the benefits of BESS in EVs, sizable advancements are wanted in battery technology, including elevated energy density, quicker charging skills, and longer lifespan. Additionally, studies and development are required to optimize the integration of BESS with the vehicle and the grid. With speedy improvements in the development of BESS and expanded investments in EV infrastructure, the total potential of battery power garage structures in electric-powered motors can be unlocked. It may no longer be the best way to accelerate the transition toward sustainable transportation; however, it provides full-size financial and environmental blessings.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cross-Border Supply Chains and Customer Satisfaction Using Conditional Decision Trees
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Increasing customer satisfaction in a globalized economy depends much on the management of supply chains across national borders. Among the challenges escalating the complexity are differences in regulatory criteria, delays in logistics, and shifting customer expectations. This paper uses conditional decision trees (CDT) to help to simplify decision-making procedures and increase operational efficiency in supply chains spanning international borders. This model evaluates critical performance indicators (KPIs) including delivery time, cost efficiency, and customer satisfaction by means of transactional data from real-time operations. The model also factors customer comfort. All of which surpasses the traditional approaches, the proposed strategy results in a 15% improvement in delivery efficiency, a 12% reduction in logistical expenses, and a 9% increase in customer satisfaction ratings. Two baseline models were under comparison with CDT. These models stood for the Random Forest (RF) and the Decision Tree Regressor (DTR). The results show, based on supply chain criteria, CDT achieves an accuracy of 94.6% compared to DTR and RF, so offering a clear performance benefit. This relates to DTR's accuracy of 89.4% and RF's accuracy of 91.80%. This kind of approach not only improves operational efficiency but also offers data applicable regarding the factors affecting customer satisfaction. These findings imply that CDT might be a breakthrough instrument in the fields of worldwide supply chain management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Lung Cancer Detection Using Radial Deep Belief and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Early identification is essential to increase the survival percentage among those affected since cancer still ranks first among all causes of death worldwide. Particularly in terms of differentiating adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), conventional diagnostic approaches sometimes find it difficult to correctly identify the several forms of lung cancer. We propose in this work a novel method combining Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with Radial Deep Belief Network (RDBN) to improve the accuracy of lung cancer picture categorization taken from the LIDC-IDRI dataset. PSO is in charge of modifying the network parameters to achieve higher performance while the RDBN design is in charge of properly capturing intricate characteristics in the pictures. Our model obtained an accuracy of 92.5% regarding the classification of non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma. Furthermore, present in our model were a 93.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> specificity and a 90.2% sensitivity. Training time was required thirty percent less since PSO techniques are more computationally efficient than traditional optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Tomato Leaf Diseases Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In this study, an automated system to detect tomato leaf diseases with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) is introduced to aid farmers in early disease identification to avert crop losses and promote yield. The dataset is multiple classes of tomato leaf diseases, and the model was trained and tuned extensively for its performance. In particular, a high training accuracy of 95.73%, and validation accuracy of 89.85% was achieved by CNN. Furthermore, the system's precision, recall, and F1 metric were around 90%, indicating the balanced system performance. The proposed CNN model is shown to be more reliable and faster than the traditional image processing techniques and hence is an appropriate choice for real time agricultural applications. The integration of modern varieties technologies in AI based approaches in agriculture which will feed productivity while maintaining Sustainability. The results indicate that the proposed system could provide an effective means for disease detection for farmers and may alleviate some of the need for chemical treatments.

articleTitle: Unleashing the Potential of Battery Algorithms for Optimal Performance in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The increasing demand for electric-powered vehicles (EVs) has brought about a growing desire for battery algorithms that can optimize battery performance. Those algorithms can substantially affect the range, charging time, and usual efficiency of EVs, making them an essential factor in the transition to a greener transportation system. However, there is nevertheless tons of potential to be unlocked in battery algorithms to enhance EV overall performance. Contemporary battery algorithms depend upon traditional management techniques, which may be restricted in their capability to adapt to changing situations and may need to utilize the skills of modern-day battery technologies fully. To absolutely unleash the capacity of battery algorithms, new procedures such as gadget mastering and artificial intelligence may be implemented. These superior strategies can examine and adapt to actual-time facts from the battery and its environment, taking into account extra correct and green control. Moreover, integrating data from diverse sensors and communiqué technology can provide an extra comprehensive understanding of the battery device, leading to higher performance and longer battery existence. It additionally allows predictive preservation, assisting in saving you from capacity disasters and amplifying the lifespan of batteries. With the aid of constantly optimizing battery algorithms, the range, charging time and typical overall performance of EVs may be drastically stepped forward, making them a possible alternative for consumers. It will, in the long run, accelerate the transition towards a sustainable and greener transportation system.

articleTitle: Multi-Connectivity Techniques in 5G Networks: Performance Analysis and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Multi-connectivity techniques in 5G networks permit the simultaneous use of more than one connection to improve network performance and reliability. These strategies involve using a couple of access technologies, such as LTE and millimeter-wave, to provide customers with more than one path to resources and offerings. This abstract discusses the performance evaluation and optimization of multi-connectivity strategies in 5G networks. The performance of multi-connectivity techniques is evaluated primarily based on parameters including community throughput, latency, and coverage. It has been proven that those techniques can enhance community overall performance by utilizing the to-be-had assets wirelessly. However, there are challenges in maintaining seamless connectivity and coping with the interactions between specific wireless technologies. Diverse answers have been proposed to optimize the performance of multi-connectivity techniques, including network choice algorithms, load balancing methods, and clever handover mechanisms. These optimizations purpose to allocate resources wi-ficaciously wireless and reduce disruptions all through handovers among one-of-a-kind connections

articleTitle: Innovations in Battery Design for Improved Cycle Durability and Flexibility in Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The increasing call for electric-powered and hybrid cars has led to the want for greater efficient and durable battery designs. In response, improvements in the battery era have targeted improving cycle sturdiness and versatility in automotive programs. One essential innovation is the use of lithium-ion batteries, which offer higher power density and longer cycle life compared to traditional lead-acid batteries. Inside the realm of lithium-ion batteries, improvements have been made in electrode materials and cell designs. For instance, using silicon-based, total anodes has substantially increased the strength density of lithium-ion batteries, allowing for longer use tiers and improved cycle existence. Additionally, advancements in battery control structures have progressed the potential to reveal and manipulate the charging and discharging of batteries, growing their usual durability and lifespan. This has caused the development of fast-changing technologies that could rate a battery to eighty in only half an hour, making it an extra handy and realistic alternative for electric car proprietors.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cost Efficiency in Cloud-Based Automation with DevOps Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Cloud automation has created a trend offering several advantages to businesses, including scalability and cost-effectiveness. Although deploying such automation in a cloud setting is fundamental, optimizing its cost efficiency proves challenging, particularly with DEVOPS techniques. DEVOPS integrates development and operations to promote collaboration and automate different parts of the software delivery process. It is also possible to elaborate the DEVOPS techniques by implementing them through cloud-based automation, which can greatly benefit both efficiency and cost. A key area for cost optimization is infrastructure management. By using DEVOPS techniques for the provisioning and deployment of resources, organizations can automate what have previously been tedious and manual processes, which can lead to lower infrastructure costs and more efficiency. Utilization of resources can be enhanced through DEVOPS techniques. Auto-scaling automatically adapts resources based on demand, while load balancing distributes workloads across resources to improve performance and costs. However, one area in which DEVOPS can dramatically enhance companies' cost efficiency is continuous monitoring and optimizing. Automated monitoring tools fire alerts notifying businesses about the most precise area where work is being done inefficiently in real-time, helping companies to save money.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Techniques for Self-Powered Body-Worn Sensors in Wireless Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Self-powered body-worn sensors are considered one of the potential candidates for health and fitness monitoring in wireless body area networks. Sensors extract energy from the human body or its environment to power themselves, making them self-contained with no external power supply, thus improving portability and wear ability. According to this, energy harvesting methods are essential for developing selfpowered body-worn sensors in WBANs. This technical paper reviews different methods of energy harvesting used for bodyworn sensors, such as Body heat, motion, ambient light harvesting, etc. It also discusses some drawbacks and limitations, such as low energy production and inconsistent energy sources. It also features some of the latest blasting techniques and technologies concerning energy recovery. Using self-powered body-worn sensors can lead to various applications and advantages in WBANs. Such uses included continuous & non-invasive health monitoring, data collection for medical research and sports performance tracking. Self-powered sensors reduce the frequency of maintenance and minimize environmental pollution caused by battery disposal.

articleTitle: Data Mining for Fraud Detection in Telecommunications: Detecting Anomalous Behaviors in Real-Time
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: In the recent past, telecom experts have been confronted with so many problems emanating from fraudulent deeds that apart from causing loss of money discredits organizations. To mitigate these problems, real-time fraud detection systems are very essential in detected those unusual and unauthorized activities. This study aims at examining how data mining can be used in the identification of the actual fraud in the telecommunication area through users' interactions in the course of which a huge amount of data is produced. In this study, the case uses different machine learning algorithms including clustering, decision trees, and anomaly detection for mapping out unusual call pattern, unauthorized access and Identity theft. To capture anomalous behavior, the research uses both time-domain and frequency domain data from different telecom networks for training and testing models. The research also intends to extend existing theories and practices of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and deep learning networks to improve accuracy and effectiveness of the sort of systems used in the detection of fraud. The performance of these models is measured in terms of accuracy in classification and prediction of fraudulent actions thereby reducing potentials false negative and false positive cases. Further, the paper outlines how these models can be integrated into existing network security architecture to assess the prospects for scalability of these solutions within a maturing fraud environment. The findings also affirm that data mining is effective in real-time monitoring and prevention of frauds as such highlighting the importance of frequent updates of the fraud detection solutions within the telecommunication sector.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of IoT and Sensor-Enabled Logistics Management for Supply Chain Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The logistics sector has become increasingly tech-driven due to the growing need for streamlined supply chain management. The Internet of Things (IoT) is a technology that has gained prominence in optimizing supply chain processes and sensor-enabled logistics management. For starters, IoT means the interconnection of certain devices with one another through The Internet to collect and transmit data in real time. The generated data can then be used to trace the location and condition of goods along the journey and monitor real-time performance from logistics operations. Sensors, however, cover everything from the temperature, humidity, and vibration of goods for their warehouse data needs. It can provide real-time actionable insights for supply chain stakeholders to make informed decisions and corrective actions by enabling IoT and sensor-enabled logistics management. Such actions will improve efficiency and reduce costs while improving customer satisfaction. IoT and sensors can also play a role in predictive maintenance, ensuring fixes or replacements are made proactively to minimize downtime disruptions in the supply chain.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Self-Aware Financial Inclusion System for Digital Society
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The continuous advancement in technology has restructured industries, due to innovations in Artificial Intelligence (AI) the financial sector endorsing astonishing transformations. This research recognizes the potential of AI in fintech for digital society while focusing on the transition toward Industry 5.0, which is based on human-AI collaboration. AI technologies, such as Artificial Generative Intelligence (AGI) and Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI), are limited in handling intricate, vigorous financial environments. ANI has improved efficiency via credit risk assessment, customer service automation, and fraud detection, whereas AGI aims for more comprehensive decision-making capabilities. ANI and AGI are creating a gap in accomplishing a truly responsive, customer-centric system as it cannot fully adapt to subtle decision-making or erratic market shifts. This paper suggests a Super Artificial Intelligence (SAl) as a promising solution to overcome limitations, standing SAI-based design for a unified nifty digital financial system. Its forward-thinking decision-making proficiencies, self-learning, and flexibility are expected to transmute financial aligned with Industry 5.0's human-centered principles by providing adaptive services, enhancing financial inclusion and personalized. The paper concludes by underscoring the importance of continuous AI validation, ethical considerations, and human oversight to ensure sustainable, secure, and customer-focused financial systems.

articleTitle: Sensor Fusion Techniques for Accurate Indoor Tracking in IoT-Based Smart Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Sensor fusion integrates data from multiple sensors to provide a more accurate, reliable, and contextual sense of the surrounding environment. So, it became a key method for correct monitoring in battery-dependent Internet of Things clever environments, especially Indoor tracking. There is only one dedicated sensor. To benefit the most from it and surround these weaknesses in complex indoor environments with wrongness. The sensor fusion methods for accurate indoor tracking in IoT-based Smart Environments are proposed to solve the problems above by integrating data from multiple sources, including Wi-Fi APs and BLE beacons, RFID readers, and IMUs. This results in a more complete and detailed view of the environment crucial for location-based applications such as asset tracking, localization, or navigation within smart buildings. There are many algorithms to fuse sensor data. The algorithms process the sensor data and give a fused result that outperforms all of these individual components. Sensor fusion in IoT-based smart environments improves indoor tracking accuracy, robustness, and scalability. It also permits real-time tracking localization of objects and people; it is the key to optimally managing smart environments. The sensor fusion method generally improves indoor tracking properties in the rapidly growing IoT-based smart environments.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Regression Algorithms in Lung Cancer Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Results of All Cancers The mortality of lung cancer is highest among both international and domestic patients. Hence, early detection and accurate prediction are essential for treatment-affecting diagnoses to improve patient outcomes. Throughout the evolution of machine learning technologies, numerous regression algorithms have been introduced to predict lung cancer using clinical data or imaging datasets. In this work, we perform a comparison analysis among linear regression, logistic regression, and all commonly used decision-tree-based methods, including Decision Trees (CART), Random Forests, and Support Vector Machines for predicting lung cancer diagnosis and prognosis. We use patient data from two hospitals, including age, smoking information, lung function tests, and imaging results, to perform the analysis. Our results suggest that random forest and support vector machines generally offer the best accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity in diagnosis and prognosis prediction. Decision tree algorithms also do but depend heavily on the feature set chosen. In addition, we show improved performance in predicting placebo response by combining different data sources. Our study demonstrates that selecting regression algorithms are critical in lung cancer prediction and that combining multiple data types can improve accuracy. Realizing this potential requires accurate prediction algorithms, which are not currently available; such information can lead to better-developed forecast models and improved lung cancer patients' diagnoses and outcomes.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Dynamic Resource Allocation in Cloud Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Cloud automation enables the dynamic management and allocation of resources in a computing environment and is one of the most common uses available. Yet despite their power when cloud systems were simple and small, traditional approaches to allocating resources have proven far less feasible lately. This scenario has also created the need for new evolution methods that will adapt to dynamic cloud environments and improve the system's overall performance. A solution to this challenge comes from machine learning, which has been increasingly used recently. ML algorithms can process vast amounts of data and identify patterns and trends to predict resource use and user needs. Deep learning helps cloud-enabled automation systems adapt in real-time to changing conditions, distribute resources efficiently and improve user experience. For example, reinforcement learning and deep learning are ML techniques that can be applied to resource allocation algorithms or demand prediction models to increase accuracy. Integrating cloud automation and machine learning brings effectiveness in dynamic resource allocation, boosting the overall performance of a system, which leads to savings, better experience, and greater flexibility in using cloud resources. Reinforcement and deep learning are machine learning techniques to optimize order allocation algorithms and enhance demand estimation models.

articleTitle: Optimizing Advertising Campaigns through Advanced Deep Learning-Driven Audience Segmentation for Enhanced Targeting and Engagement
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The present work discusses the utilization of deep learning techniques for precise dividing the audience for advertising in order to increase efficiency and effectiveness of campaigns. Hence, the paper employs a diverse dataset of consumers' demographic data, purchase history, social media activity, and reviews and design a hybrid deep learning model using CNN, RNN-LSTM, and attention mechanisms. In all the assessment measurements of accuracy, precision, recall, and Fl-score, this model offers better results compared with the old-shoot segmentation methods. The performance analysis depicts great enhancements in CTR, conversion rate, as well as ROAS all of which highlight a superior engagement of the ads. Indeed, the outcome points to the effectiveness of deep learning in digital marketing that can provide clients with more efficient advertising tools. Nonetheless, the issues regarding computational capabilities and ethical concerns pose viable and useful innovations and solutions, thus contributing to the progression of deep learning theories in audience segmentation and advertising.

articleTitle: Towards Reliable and Energy-Efficient Communication Protocols for Wireless Body Area Networks in Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Wireless body area networks are an attractive technology for measuring health data in medical applications. Several challenges exist in designing and implementing such reliable, energy-efficient communication protocols for these networks. This new strategy solution strategy is based on a hybrid communication protocol that simultaneously obtains the positive aspects of centralized and distributed structures. By centralizing network maintenance and control functions such as health monitoring of nodes and transmission control, the proposed protocol supports reliable data transmission with minimal energy consumption in WBANs. This reduces the overhead and collisions, giving the network better reliability. Unlike other protocols mentioned where the data flow from the sensor node to the central node is at least distributed, in our case, a few nodes send their data at a time to the Central Node. It enables low-power communication since nodes only need to wake up during their allotted transmission time slot. Through simulations, we demonstrate that the new protocol surpasses existing protocols in reliability and energy consumption performance. It can also help to minimize the energy consumption of WBAN nodes, which makes it an appropriate candidate for long-time medical monitoring applications. All in all, this work helps to pave the way for the efficient use of WBANs in a wide range of medical applications that require robustness and low-energy communications.

articleTitle: Smart Lighting Systems for Energy Efficiency Using IoT and Sensor Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Smart Lighting Systems for Energy Efficiency via Internet of Things (IoT) and Sensor Technologies A novel method of attaining energy efficiency is combining IoT with sensor technology. The emergence of the IOT given go up to intelligent lighting systems that can leverage sensors, data analytics, and connectivity means for energy optimization. Their purpose is to adjust lighting levels automatically regarding occupancy, daylight availability, and time of day to save significant amounts of power. The sensors are wireless; hence, they are battery-powered IoT devices that measure the ambient light level at the location where they were installed. It also measures movement in their range and temperature readings for an office or conference area, enabling smart lighting systems to adapt to local conditions while minimizing energy wastage. This mechanism of collecting real-time data and analyzing the same gives us insights on patterns or preferences in lighting usage thus can be customized for different type's timings. This increases the effective use of artificial lighting and ensures it takes advantage of natural light availability. In addition to this, these systems can also integrate with other smart building technologies like heating and cooling systems for a well-rounded approach to energy management. The lighting control from mobile devices enhances building owners' and managers' convenience and to manage their property features remotely.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Protecting Privacy in Big Data Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Due to the big data era, the use of cloud computing and Internet of Things devices has increased tremendously, which has resulted in the mass collection of personal data. This caused major privacy protection and safety issues, as sensitive personal data could be exploited and misused. Data encryption and similar techniques have largely needed to be improved as a privacy-protecting solution. A new approach to overcome the privacy and security issues in big data networks is federated learning. Federated Learning is a distributed approach to learning in which machine learning models are trained locally on each device (e.g., phone), and the raw data never leaves the local devices to reach a central server. With this device, however, only model updates are sent while the private data continues to be stored locally on the devices for privacy protection. FL has several benefits compared to normal privacy protection methods, such as reducing the risks of data breaches and minimizing computational and communication costs. In addition, FL allows better data management and greater control over personal data as users are involved in training. FL can be an important building block for privacy and security in large data networks, and it has been adopted by most of the major technology companies as part of their applications. They still have to solve problems like efficient convergence of the model, heterogeneous data and so on. FL is still being prepared for practical use in big data networks and needs more research based on its development to protect privacy.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Deep and Machine Learning Models in Knee Osteoarthritis Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common type of arthritis characterised by recent cartilaginous joint destruction and alteration of bone, ligaments and synovial fluid. This paper presents a brief knowledge about the knee OA, including its cause and effect, assessment, signs, prevalence, and the methods of managing it together with Different algorithms like Decision Tree, Random Forest, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) Naive Bayes and CNN. The dataset was collected from GitHub which was from OAI dataset which consists of csv datasets. The accuracy of the algorithms were 85%, 89%, 88%, 95% and 85%. Out of five algorithms, the best algorithm were Naïve Bayes and Random Forest algorithm.

articleTitle: Integrating Dynamic Access Control in Hybrid Cloud Environments for Enhanced Security and Load Balancing
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Hybrid cloud environments come into play more each month, this service is becoming increasingly important for security and load balancing. Hybrid cloud environments are too fluid to manage with traditional access control methods and load-balancing solutions. This is where dynamic access control integration comes in. Dynamic access control is a process that enables organizations to define and enforce access controls based on the context of the request, not merely user identities. This could be applied in a hybrid cloud environment to implement access controls based on the whereabouts of users, the kind of data, and the threat level. This is intended to add an extra layer of security as we can limit the users who have permission to access specific resources. You can add dynamic access control to your load-balancing solutions for resource efficiency and performance improvements. It also reduces the possibility of service outage, as more accurate granular access control based on lower visibility to higher certain users making fewer requests at a time than another set can simplify algorithms that tombstone or down-replicated out-of-date servers and thus carve their load across racks of machines.

articleTitle: Cyber Threat Intelligence Extraction Using Text Mining Techniques for Proactive Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) is valuable in gaining insight into current tactics, techniques and procedures used by the adversaries in a cyber attack. In this work, a new framework applying GAN for classifying tactics and techniques from unstructured CTI data is presented. The described approach combines two models by addressing the link between high-level tactics and low-level middle-level technologies by using a hierarchical method and CNNs based on attention mechanisms. Encoders from the specific subject fields as well as high-quality preprocessing methods are used to transform the initial information from the CTI reports into the set of features which could be easily utilized. Thus, the adversarial training mechanism ensures that the generated data are reasonable and semantically correct to promote enhanced classification. The proposed framework was tested on several datasets, and the experimental results demonstrated higher accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score than other relevant approaches. The imposed hierarchy on GAN improves system's realism in feature representation, supporting CTI analysis and cyberattack behavior comprehension. This approach establishes the groundwork for the implementation of large-scale, preventive attitude into the cybersecurity models, and arms analysts with information obtained from difficult and chaotic data feedstocks.

articleTitle: IOT and Sensor-Based Flood Monitoring and Warning Systems for Disaster Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The Internet of Things, which has sensors for monitoring floods and generating alerts, reflects the most contemporary use-case of these solutions in disaster management. Using linked devices and sensors, these systems gather real-time information concerning water levels, weather aspects, and other environmental factors associated with flooding. This data can now produce precise flood forecasts and alerts, giving communities the information they need for large weather events with a better idea of when disasters may strike. Advantages of IOT and sensor-based flood monitoring systems: Sensor cadmium selenium photocells, sharp water & infrared sensors, which include water level sensors, rain gauges, and temperature sensors in places exposed to floods. They do this by involving sensors installed throughout the city that monitor water levels or rainfall and can relay fluctuations to a central box. The data is then processed by sophisticated algorithms, resulting in flood forecasts and alerts that can be accessed via web-based platforms or mobile apps. One significant benefit of these systems is real-time flood data with accurate results that help communities evacuate and other disaster mitigation actions. These systems can also be linked to established emergency response systems that serve as an information source for graduate disaster management. These sensors and IOT-based flood monitoring systems also make for great innovative Disaster Management tools that will increase awareness, leading to better preparedness and response time between the occurrences of a natural disaster like floods with communities.

articleTitle: Optimizing Telemedicine Services for Rural Women: A Decision Tree-Based Heap Optimizer Approach for Predictive Healthcare Delivery
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Women living in rural areas still have a great difficulty gaining access to healthcare especially in underdeveloped areas where the infrastructure for medical treatment is limited. By means of remotely available healthcare services, telemedicine has become a possibly useful solution to close this gap; still, the optimisation of these services to generate better outcomes is a continuous challenge. Even if telemedicine is becoming more and more popular, women living in rural areas still sometimes face challenges including limited health resources, socioeconomic problems, and poor internet access. Therefore, much sought for are effective optimisation models that can predict the needs of healthcare and enhance the provision of services to this particular group. This work attempts to provide a Decision Tree-based Heap Optimiser (DTHO) for use in rural women's telemedicine service prediction and optimisation. Using decision tree learning, the DTHO method classifies healthcare needs depending on past data. Moreover, used are heap-based approaches for effective resource distribution. Using data from surveys on telemedicine use and rural healthcare, the predictive model was developed by means of analysis. The model maximised resource allocation by 30%, so allowing a more efficient provision of telemedicine services. For identifying healthcare needs, it also attained an accuracy of 85%. Reducing service delays by 20–25 percent enabled the heap-based optimiser to increase patient satisfaction by 20%.

articleTitle: The Role of Cyber-Physical Systems in Revolutionizing Transportation: From Connected Cars to Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Cyber-physical systems have technologically advanced the transportation industry with their ability to connect physical systems with virtual functions. A cyber-physical system uses real-time data generation and communication technologies to make transportation systems safer, more efficient, more sustainable and more reliable. Connected cars are one of the primary use cases of CPS in transportation. They utilize sensors, cameras, and internet connectivity to capture information regarding road conditions, traffic patterns, and other drivers on the road. This information is then communicated to the backend system for analysis and decision-making to enhance safety or alleviate traffic congestion. It has also contributed towards developing independent vehicles. They employ ACH and CPS technologies to drive on roads driving without the need for human intervention. This could lead to a huge reduction in human error-related accidents and improve the efficiency of transportation. CPS also helps build smart transportation systems or link multiple modes of transport to escape congestion and reduce travel time. For example, it involves the integration of different modes of transportation, such as public transit, ride-sharing services and self-driving cars, to minimize travel time while maximizing usage. CPS has revolutionized the transport sector into a more connected, effective and secures system.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Effect of Eco-Friendly Branding on Consumer Purchasing Decisions on Sustainability in Marketing using Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Background: Consumer buying behaviour is increasingly influenced by eco-friendly branding, thus sustainable practices are starting to take front stage in contemporary marketing plans. Companies under increased demand to link their brands with sustainable ideas as consumers become more conscious of the effects they have on the environment. Contribution: This study investigates how environmentally friendly branding influences purchasing decisions keeping customer attitudes as well as behaviour changes in mind. Findings: A comprehensive survey was given to 1,500 persons total throughout the duration of the research and statistical analysis was done with assistance from a simulation tool in order to evaluate changes in consumer sentiment and purchase behaviour. Results: Based on the findings, 48 percent of the participants were ready to pay extra for environmentally friendly products and 72 percent showed an increased tendency to buy from companies deemed to be such. Moreover, sixty-four percent of respondents claimed that environmental regulations greatly affected their brand loyalty. These findings emphasise the significance of adding sustainability into marketing plans to establish confidence in a company and to establish long-term ties with contented consumers.

articleTitle: Deep CNN Architectures for Predicting Malignant Bone Tumors from MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: A malignant bone tumor is a rare but aggressive form of cancer that requires surgical removal before metastasizing and compromising other organs. Pre-operative localization of these tumors is key for surgery. However, current imaging methods applied in a standard MRI protocol might only sometimes be able to pinpoint the exact nature of certain types. To solve this problem, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) were introduced as a possible way to predict benign and malignant bone tumors detected on MRI. Deep CNNs are powerful machine learning algorithms that can learn complex features from data and the classifier without explicit feature engineering. They are especially good for processing large, highly apparent medical images, as found in MRI scans. Though many state-of-the-art deep CNN architectures have been suggested for automatically detecting malignant bone tumors, they performed with different success rates. This architecture is employed by structures that include various convolutions, pooling, and nonlinear activations, and it helps the models learn spatially or temporally associated features in MRI images. These deep CNN architectures were performed with high accuracy and sensitivity in predicting malignant bone tumors from MRI scans. It could enhance the early detection and treatment of these deadly cancers. Future work in strengthening and fine-tuning these deep CNN architectures could improve the accuracy and efficacy of predicting malignant bone tumors from MRI scans, which may translate to better clinical outcomes.

articleTitle: Real-Time Traffic Sign Detection and Recognition Using Faster R-CNN with VGG16 Backbone
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Real-time detection and recognition of traffic signs is an inevitable part of advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous driving. Here in this paper, we come up with a traffic sign detection system which employs Faster R-CNN as its framework and VGG16 for extracting features. This system successfully implements traffic sign detection and classification with high accuracy and speed even in unfavorable conditions like illumination changes, occlusion, and complex background. The Region Proposal Network successfully filters down the possible regions of interest, and the VGG16 as a backbone, extracts more features useful in traffic sign detection. In order to justify the proposed model, we use treat public databases such as the German Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark (GTSDB). The test set results of the proposed system are a precision of 93.4, a recall of 92.1, an F1-score of 92.7, and an mAP of 94.5. In addition, optimizations are included for real-time functionality with mean inference time equal on average 88 ms. Comparing it with other models such as YOLOv3 and SSD shows that the proposed system is more accurate than it is faster. Based on the obtained results, it can be argued that the described approach is perfect for real traffic sign detection in ITS.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Serverless Architecture for Cloud Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: Server less architecture has become increasingly used in cloud computers since it is highly scalable and affordable and allows for the rapid deployment of services. However, no one has abused server less architecture yet, especially from a cloud operations and management perspective. This paper will explore the benefits of cloud automation using server less architecture. Cloud Automation: techniques that replace manual, repetitive activities in the cloud, such as provisioning resources, configuring applications, and monitoring performance. Server less architecture allows organizations to automate more processes and become more operationally efficient. The server less architecture frees developers from the responsibility of maintaining and managing servers. This directly reduces the overhead on IT teams. It allows them to spend time on more important things like creating and deploying applications. Moreover, server less architecture automatically scales resources based on demand, facilitating optimal utilization and cost-effectiveness. In addition, cloud automation using server less architecture allows you to combine different tools and services, one example being event-driven services that play nicely with databases or third-party services. This, in turn, enables a more holistic and cohesive solution for cloud operations automation.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Approaches for Fastag Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The growth of electronic toll collection has led to more fraud, especially when serious drivers use FASTags to ease traffic congestion to avoid repeat fraud. This study highlights the urgent need for effective enforcement of FASTag fraud. Our system is designed to detect and prevent false phone numbers by analysing key features such as money transfer, vehicle type, phone line type, and location. Construct complex fraud models using advanced techniques in machine learning algorithms: KNN, XG Boost, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Naive Bayes Classifier, Gaussian Naive Bayes, ANN, SVM Classifier etc. This model has shown great success with ANN achieving the highest accuracy (99.88%) and F1 score (99.93%). It helps in creating a safer and more reliable system by increasing the validity of FASTag transactions. By using these algorithms, the aim is to reduce fraud and increase the integrity and security of the FASTag system. In addition to increasing the security of electronic toll collection, the system also offers solutions that will reduce FASTag fraud and ensure fairness in payments across vehicle models.

articleTitle: IoT and Sensor-Enabled Predictive Maintenance for Industrial Machinery: Analysis of the Manufacturing Sector
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: The sector area is free to move toward utilizing the Internet of Things and sensor-enabled predictive maintenance; these days, this has changed into a preached scenario. This is a sophisticated, sensor-based predictive maintenance system with sensors and data analytics to monitor the health of industrial machines at production plants and predict their failure so that companies can cut downtime due to machine failures. Real-time Monitoring of Equipment: IoT is enabled with sensors that predict maintenance operations and help to understand the functioning status in real-time for any nature or size of equipment, from a small/massive engine to a storage tank tailored to wind turbines. By doing this, they can identify any issues or unusual behaviors before they develop into more serious and expensive problems, allowing them to schedule maintenance activities. Moreover, this allows for the sensor data to be reviewed and correlated to see patterns and trends on when equipment might break down so that a pre-emptive maintenance action could have been done instead. This technology will be extremely useful for the manufacturing sector, where equipment failure results in high costs and losses due to production downtime.

articleTitle: Mitigating DDoS Attacks in Software-Defined Networks (SDN) Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Automation and Computation (AUTOCOM)
abstract: SDN stands for Software Defined Network, which describes a new way of network architecture that separates the control plane from the data plane and thus brings centralized control and programmability over the áreas of networking. This centralized-controlled feature gave SDN the advantage that DDoS attacks can crash the network, causing it to be non-functional. In the traditional DDoS mitigation techniques, rate limiting and traffic filtering are highly common; SDN is a dynamic network that changes rapidly, and such practices cannot eliminate DDoS attacks efficiently. One possible solution to this problem is employing machine learning methods to detect and prevent DDoS attacks in SDN. These methods utilize the capturing of network traffic and performance metrics from different components, such as SDN switches and controllers, to build machine learning models by training them. It can accurately detect and identify DDoS attacks based on patterns and anomalies in network traffic after those models have been trained. Integration of Machine Learning-based DDoS Mitigation Techniques in Software-Defined Networks can help Operators protect their networks from DDoS attacks proactively and effectively.
